rows.acip: ,GSUM PA NI, SU GA TA'I SGRA SPANGS PA DANG RTOGS PA GNYIS LA BSHAD DU YOD PAS SPANGS PA PHUN TSOGS KYI YON TAN NI, SKYES BU GZUGS LEGS PA BZHIN DU NYON MONGS PA'I SGRIB PA ZAD PAR SPANGS PAS LEGS PA'AM MDZES PAR GSHEGS PA DANG , RIMS NAD LEGS PAR BYANG BA BZHIN DU NYON MONGS PA'I DBANG GIS SLAR 'KHOR BAR MI LDOG PAR GSHEGS PA DANG , BUM PA LEGS PAR GANG BA BZHIN DU NYON MONGS PA CAN MA YIN PA'I MA RIG PA ZAD PAR SPANGS PAS MA LUS PAR GSHEGS PAS BDE BAR GSHEGS PA'O, , BDE BA NI LEGS PA SOGS DANG , GSHEGS PA NI DE'I BDAG NYID DU SON PA'O,
rows.wylie: gsum pa ni, su ga ta'i sgra spangs pa dang rtogs pa gnyis la bshad du yod pas spangs pa phun tshogs kyi yon tan ni, skyes bu gzugs legs pa bzhin du nyon mongs pa'i sgrib pa zad par spangs pas legs pa'am mdzes par gshegs pa dang , rims nad legs par byang ba bzhin du nyon mongs pa'i dbang gis slar 'khor bar mi ldog par gshegs pa dang , bum pa legs par gang ba bzhin du nyon mongs pa can ma yin pa'i ma rig pa zad par spangs pas ma lus par gshegs pas bde bar gshegs pa'o, , bde ba ni legs pa sogs dang , gshegs pa ni de'i bdag nyid du son pa'o
rows.english: The Sanskrit word Sugata [Those Who have Gone to Well-Being] can be explained in two ways. We can explain it in reference to either the things which an Enlightened Being has eliminated, or in reference to the things which he or she has realized. First I will explain it in terms of that excellent virtue an Enlightened Being possess of having totally eliminated every single bad quality there is. Because an Enlightened Being has completely cleaned Himself of all the obstacles which are related to bad thoughts, we can say that he has gone well, or beautifully, and is like someone who has an well-formed body. Because he will never have to return back to this cycle of suffering life by force of things poisoned with the afflictions of the mind, we can say that he has gone like someone who has been completely cured, or made well, from an illness. And because he has totally removed all of those kinds of ignorance which are not related to the mental afflictions, we can say that he has totally gone like a vase which is well-filled. It is in this way that we call such a being One Who Has Gone to Well-Being. We say "well-being" to refer to the different qualities described above with the word "well", and we say "gone" to indicate that these beings have gone to the nature which embodies those very qualities.

rows.acip: ,DE NAS BYAMS PA DANG SNYING RJE'I RTZA BA CAN GYI BYANG CHUB KYI MCHOG TU SEMS BSKYED PA LA 'KHOR LO SGYUR BA'I RGYAL PO SPYAN 'DREN PA'I GNAS KHANG SOGS BYI DOR BYED PA BZHIN DU 'GAL RKYEN SGRIB PA BSHAGS PA DANG , MTHUN RKYEN TSOGS BSAGS NAS BYANG CHUB KYI SEMS GZUNG DGOS PA'I SNGA MA LE'U GNYIS PA DANG , PHYI MA LE'U GSUM PAS BSTAN TO,
rows.wylie: de nas byams pa dang snying rje'i rtsa ba can gyi byang chub kyi mchog tu sems bskyed pa la 'khor lo sgyur ba'i rgyal po spyan 'dren pa'i gnas khang sogs byi dor byed pa bzhin du 'gal rkyen sgrib pa bshags pa dang , mthun rkyen tshogs bsags nas byang chub kyi sems gzung dgos pa'i snga ma le'u gnyis pa dang , phyi ma le'u gsum pas bstan to
rows.english: You must go about developing the wish to achieve supreme enlightenment, that wish whose very root is love and compassion, in the same way that you would go about preparing to welcome a King who ruled the entire world by cleaning your house, and so on. You will be able to acquire this wish by purifying all of the factors which obstruct your spiritual realizations, and gathering together the power of good deeds which promote them. These two subjects are covered respectively in the second and third chapters.

rows.acip: ,DANG PO NI, BYANG CHUB KYI SEMS GNYIS BSGOM PA LA 'BAD PAR RIGS TE, DMYAL BA'I RGYU LA SOGS PA'I SDIG PA MI BZAD PA DE NI RDZOGS PA'I BYANG CHUB KYI SEMS MIN PA DGE BA GZHAN GANG GIS ZIL GYIS GNON PAR 'GYUR TE GANG GIS KYANG ZIL GYIS GNON MI NUS PA'I PHYIR RO, , DON DAM SEMS BSKYED KYIS SGRIB PA'I SA BON SPONG BA'I NUS PA YOD PA 'DIR BSHAD BYA'I GTZO BO MA YIN GYI, 'DIR NI KUN RDZOB SEMS BSKYED KYIS NGAN 'GRO'I RGYU SNGAR BSAGS 'DAG CING PHYI MA RGYUN GCOD PAR BYED PA'I PHAN YON BSTAN TO,

rows.english: Making great efforts to practice the two forms of the wish for enlightenment is something which is very right to do. This is because we have committed negative deeds of dreadful strength, deeds that would cause us to be born into the hells, or the like. And what kind of goodness could there ever be, other than the wish for total enlightenment, that could overwhelm them? The answer is that there is no such other goodness. The main point being mentioned here is not the fact that the ultimate form of the wish has the power to eliminate the seeds for spiritual obstacles. The intent rather is to indicate the benefit of the wish where, in its "deceptive" form, the wish functions to clear away those causes already created which would take one to the births of misery, and also functions to prevent the continued creation of these causes in the future.

rows.acip: ,GNYIS PA NI, BDAG NI NGAN 'GRO'I 'JIGS PAS RNAM SKRAG NAS SMON LAM GYI STOBS CAN GYI RGYAL SRAS KUN TU BZANG PO LA BDAG NYID 'BUL BAS 'JIGS PA LAS BDAG BSKYAB TU GSOL ZHES PA'O, , 'JAM PA'I DBYANGS LA BDAG NYID KYIS TE GZHAN GYIS BSKUL BA MA YIN PAR SEMS DANG BAS BDAG GI LUS 'DI DBUL BAR BGYI'O, , LHUN GYIS GRUB PA DANG RGYUN MI 'CHAD PA GNYIS KYIS GZHAN DON MDZAD PA'I THUGS RJE'I SPYOD PA MA 'KHRUL BA CAN SPYAN RAS GZIGS MGON DE LA YANG 'JIGS PAS NYAMS THAG PA'I NGA ROS 'O DOD 'BOD DO, , JI LTAR ZHE NA, SDIG LDAN BDAG LA BSKYAB TU GSOL ZHES SO, , DE BZHIN DU BYANG CHUB SEMS DPA' 'PHAGS PA NAM MKHA'I SNYING PO DANG SA'I SNYING PO DAG DANG NI BYAMS PA DANG SGRIB PA RNAM SEL SOGS THUGS RJE CHE MGON THAMS CAD LA SKYABS SU TSOL ZHING , SNYING NAS 'O DOD 'BOD PAS SKYABS SHIG CES PA'O, , PHYAG NA RDO RJE GANG ZHIG MTHONG NA GSHIN RJE'I PHO NYA DMYAL SRUNGS LA SOGS SEMS CAN LA SDANG BA RNAMS SKRAG NAS PHYOGS BZHIR 'BYER PAR BYED PA RDO RJE CAN LA YANG SKYABS SU MCHI'O,
rows.wylie: gnyis pa ni, bdag ni ngan 'gro'i 'jigs pas rnam skrag nas smon lam gyi stobs can gyi rgyal sras kun tu bzang po la bdag nyid 'bul bas 'jigs pa las bdag bskyab tu gsol zhes pa'o, , 'jam pa'i dbyangs la bdag nyid kyis te gzhan gyis bskul ba ma yin par sems dang bas bdag gi lus 'di dbul bar bgyi'o, , lhun gyis grub pa dang rgyun mi 'chad pa gnyis kyis gzhan don mdzad pa'i thugs rje'i spyod pa ma 'khrul ba can spyan ras gzigs mgon de la yang 'jigs pas nyams thag pa'i nga ros 'o dod 'bod do, , ji ltar zhe na, sdig ldan bdag la bskyab tu gsol zhes so, , de bzhin du byang chub sems dpa' 'phags pa nam mkha'i snying po dang sa'i snying po dag dang ni byams pa dang sgrib pa rnam sel sogs thugs rje che mgon thams cad la skyabs su tshol zhing , snying nas 'o dod 'bod pas skyabs shig ces pa'o, , phyag na rdo rje gang zhig mthong na gshin rje'i pho nya dmyal srungs la sogs sems can la sdang ba rnams skrag nas phyogs bzhir 'byer par byed pa rdo rje can la yang skyabs su mchi'o
rows.english: I feel absolute terror over the fears of the lower realms, and so I offer myself to the Excellent One (Samantabadra), that son of the Victors who possesses the power of prayers, and beg him to protect me from these fears. I myself--that is, without the urging of anyone else at all--offer this body of mine as well to Gentle Voice (Manjushri), with thoughts of great faith. And I call out in the voice from a desperate and frightening situation, I cry out, to that one who accomplishes the aims of others in two ways--with perfect spontaneity and in an uninterrupted flow: to the one who lives in compassion, who is free of all error, to the savior--whose name is Loving Eyes (Avalokiteshvara). And how is it that I cry out? In the words, "I beg you to protect me, a person who has committed great bad deeds." Just so do I seek protection in all those saviors whose hearts are filled with great compassion: those realized bodhisattvas such as the pair named "Essence of Space" (Akashagarba) and "Essence of Earth" (Kshitigarba), and so too Loving One (Maitreya), and the Ender of Obstacles (Nivarana Vishkambi). "I cry out, from my heart, so please, protect me." And finally I take refuge in the One with the Diamond, in the Holder of the Diamond (Vajrapani). When those full of hate living beings--when those such as the messengers of death or the hellguards--catch sight of him, they are filled with fear, and are forced to flee in every direction.

rows.english: How the wish achieves the goals of others we will cover in three steps as well, describing how it has the power to remove the sufferings of living beings, how it has the power to remove the obstacles that cause these sufferings, and finally how it has the power to accomplish all help and happiness. The first of these three has five parts of its own: descriptions of how the wish destroys the Lord of Death within every living being; how it destroys poverty; how it destroys illness; how it destroys the general suffering of the cycle of life; and, more particularly, how it destroys the sufferings of the lower realms.

rows.english: As Master Shantideva's text explains, there are certain preliminaries that must be fulfilled before one can develop the wish for enlightenment. We must purify ourselves of the obstacles which are factors that work against being able to develop the wish, and we must gather together all the factors that are conducive to reaching it. You should understand that this process, of undertaking all the preliminaries and then reaching the wish itself, is the very highest way of all to get the essence out of having achieved this human body and mind, with all their spiritual leisure and fortune. As such we must make great efforts in the practice of these preliminaries.

rows.acip: DE BAS NA NYON MONGS PA DANG SHES BYA'I SGRIB PA MTHA' DAG BSAL BA'I PHYIR DU LHAG MTHONG BSKYED DGOS LA DE YANG SNGON DU ZHI GNAS BSGRUB DGOS PAS ZHI GNAS SKYE BA'I GEGS LOG PA'I LAM 'DOD PA'I RNAM RTOG SOGS MTHA' DAG LAS SEMS BSLAN TE, SPONG BA'I 'DU BYED BRGYAD KYI SGO NAS YANG DAG PA'I DMIGS PA LA RTAG PAR YANG BDAG GIS SEMS MNYAM PAR BZHAG PAR BYA'O, , MDOR NA ZHI GNAS THUN MONG BA SGRUB TSUL RGYAS PAR NYAN THOS KYI SA LAS GSUNGS PA DANG , THUN MONG MA YIN PA'I BSGRUB TSUL GZHUNG 'DI DANG SLOB DPON KA MA LA SHI LAS SGOM RIM NAS GSUNGS PA LTAR SHES PAR BYAS NAS, ZHI GNAS SGOM PA'I PHAN YON DANG , MA SGOM PA'I NYES DMIGS BSAMS NAS SEMS GNAS PA'I THABS DGU LA SOGS PAS TING NGE 'DZIN BSGOM PA LA 'BAD PAR BYA ZHING , RGYAS PAR PHA ROL TU PHYIN PA'I LAM GYI RIM PA CHE CHUNG LAS GSUNGS PA LTAR SHES PAR BYA'O,
rows.wylie: de bas na nyon mongs pa dang shes bya'i sgrib pa mtha' dag bsal ba'i phyir du lhag mthong bskyed dgos la de yang sngon du zhi gnas bsgrub dgos pas zhi gnas skye ba'i gegs log pa'i lam 'dod pa'i rnam rtog sogs mtha' dag las sems bslan te, spong ba'i 'du byed brgyad kyi sgo nas yang dag pa'i dmigs pa la rtag par yang bdag gis sems mnyam par bzhag par bya'o, , mdor na zhi gnas thun mong ba sgrub tshul rgyas par nyan thos kyi sa las gsungs pa dang , thun mong ma yin pa'i bsgrub tshul gzhung 'di dang slob dpon ka ma la shi las sgom rim nas gsungs pa ltar shes par byas nas, zhi gnas sgom pa'i phan yon dang , ma sgom pa'i nyes dmigs bsams nas sems gnas pa'i thabs dgu la sogs pas ting nge 'dzin bsgom pa la 'bad par bya zhing , rgyas par pha rol tu phyin pa'i lam gyi rim pa che chung las gsungs pa ltar shes par bya'o
rows.english: And so it is, that in order to clear away all the obstacles--both those that relate to the mental afflictions and those that block a knowledge of all things--I must learn to develop the special vision of reality. To do this, I must first learn to develop meditative quietude. And for this, I must collect my mind, to avoid the path that errs; that is, to avoid the useless thoughts of desire and so on which act to prevent me from reaching quietude. I must then use the eight factors of eliminating the problems to meditation, in order to place my thoughts always in balanced meditation upon an object that's correct. [The eight factors are: 1) an interest in learning to meditate; 2) effort which delights in meditating; 3) a kind of faith which believes in the benefits of meditation; 4) a pleasant feeling of self-control of body and mind in meditation; 5) recollection, which helps one to avoid losing the object being meditated upon; 6) awareness, which watches to see if either mental restlessness or dullness are occurring; 7) the thought to take action, which applies meditational antidotes in the mind when necessary; and 8) the thought to leave things alone, when restlessness and dullness have been shut off, and the mind is focused correctly.] To summarize, we must undertake to learn in greater detail the shared method of achieving meditative quietude as it is found in the Levels of Listeners, as well as the unique method of achieving this quietude as it is found in the present root

rows.english: But your example does not hold true. A lamp is not something which illuminates itself, because it is not something which is the object illuminated by it. There is no need for it to illuminate itself, and it could never do so anyway. If it could, then darkness too shroud both itself and other objects. This though could never be, for the reason that there is no such thing as darkness shrouding darkness. If it did shroud darkness, then it would be like shrouding a vase with a piece of cloth, and we would be unable to see the darkness itself. For these points I am enlarging upon statements found in the Root Text on Wisdom [by the realized being Nagarjuna].

rows.english: The wisdom which realizes emptiness is, moreover, the antidote for the darkness of both the mental-affliction obstacles and the obstacles to knowledge. How could it ever be then that--if you hoped to achieve quickly the state of omniscience, the state where you end finally both the obstacles--you would neglect to go and meditate upon emptiness? Without this, you would never be able to eliminate even the seeds of the mental-affliction obstacles.

rows.english: "When all these karmic obstacles had befallen him, there was some karma still remaining. These led him to a birth in the days when the Destroyer of the Foe, the Totally Enlightened One, the Buddha named Immaculate Shining Light, was teaching in the world, and he took ordination in His way. He made incredible efforts, exerting himself with the same effort that a person would if his hair had caught on fire, for sixty thousand periods each made of a hundred periods of ten million years each. And yet he was unable to reach even the level known as 'mastery,' which leads into the realization of selflessness. He spent many hundreds and thousands of lifetimes as a person with the dullest of intellect.

rows.wylie: rigs kyi bu de'i tshe de'i dus na, dge slong chos smra ba spyod pa'i blo gros zhes bya ba de gzhan zhig yin pa snyam du sems na de snyam du mi blta ste, de ci'i phyir zhe na, nga ni dge slong chos smra ba spyod pa'i blo gros zhes bya bar gyur te, nga yang de lta bu'i thabs phra mos de la ma dad pa'i sems bskyed de, las kyi sgrib pa mngon par 'du byas pas sems can dmyal ba dag tu lhung bar gyur te
rows.english: "Listen, o child of noble family. You may think that the other monk, the one named Intellect, also a teacher of the Dharma, was just any person at all. But don't think that way. Why do I say this? Because it is I myself who was that teacher, the one named Intellect. And it was I who--due to some small incident--came to lose my faith. It was I who created the karmic obstacle. And it was I who, because of it, fell down to hell.

rows.english: "Listen to me, o child of noble family. Speaking in a way that will split up other people is a great karmic obstacle. Listen, o my child. Anyone who wants to avoid this obstacle must never feel anger about what others may do. They must trust in all that others do. They must think to themselves, 'I cannot know what this other person is really thinking. It is a difficult thing to understand all that others do.' They must come to develop this way of thinking.

rows.english: It is because dependent things do not exist as things which have any nature of being ultimate that we can speak of that which does not have any nature of being ultimate. The point here is that "ultimate" refers to anything which, when you focus on and meditate upon it, your spiritual obstacles are brought to an end. Dependent things though cannot be described as such, since they do not have the power to help you purify yourself of your spiritual obstacles if you focus on and meditate upon them.

rows.wylie: ji ltar zhe na, gzhan dbang kun brtags kyis stong pa la dmigs nas bsgoms pas sgrib pa dag bar 'gyur bar shes pa na, de lta na chos can gzhan dbang la yang dmigs dgos pas de yang rnam par dag pa'i dmigs par 'gyur bas don dam par 'gyur ro snyam du dogs pa skye la kun brtags la de 'dra ba'i dogs pa med pa'i phyir ro,
rows.english: Why is this the case? Suppose that a person came to an understanding that they could purify themselves of their spiritual obstacles by focussing on, and then meditating upon, the fact that dependent things are empty of [certain] constructs. It is possible then that they might entertain the thought that--because to go through this process they had to focus upon dependent things as an example--then these same dependent things would be objects of [the path of] total purity. This in turn would mean that these dependent things were ultimate. A person would not though entertain this same thought about constructs.

rows.acip: 'O NA RANG LUGS LA SGRIB GNYIS KYI DRI MA SPONG TSUL JI LTAR BYED SNYAM NA, BDAG MED PHRA RAGS GSUM RIM PA BZHIN DU THOS BSAM GYIS GTAN LA PHAB NAS SGOM BYUNG GIS BSGOMS PAS MNGON SUM DU MTHONG BA NA NYON MONGS PA'I SGRIB PA DANG , SHES SGRIB RAGS PA DANG , SHES SGRIB PHRA MO GSUM RTZA BA NAS ZAD PAR BYED NUS ZHES STON PA YIN PAS, DNGOS SMRA BA 'DOD PA LTAR DRI MA BDEN GRUB KHAS BLANGS NAS SPONG BA MIN GYI, DRI MA BDEN MED BSGOMS NAS DRI MA SPONG BA YIN NO ZHES RANG LUGS KYI SGRIB GNYIS SPONG TSUL GTZO BOR STON PA YIN,
rows.wylie: 'o na rang lugs la sgrib gnyis kyi dri ma spong tshul ji ltar byed snyam na, bdag med phra rags gsum rim pa bzhin du thos bsam gyis gtan la phab nas sgom byung gis bsgoms pas mngon sum du mthong ba na nyon mongs pa'i sgrib pa dang , shes sgrib rags pa dang , shes sgrib phra mo gsum rtsa ba nas zad par byed nus zhes ston pa yin pas, dngos smra ba 'dod pa ltar dri ma bden grub khas blangs nas spong ba min gyi, dri ma bden med bsgoms nas dri ma spong ba yin no zhes rang lugs kyi sgrib gnyis spong tshul gtso bor ston pa yin
rows.english: "Well then," you may think to yourself, "how do we in our own position describe the process by which one eliminates the various impurities?" It has been taught that: One can gain the ability to put a total end to the three--that is, to the obstacles of the mental afflictions, to the gross obstacles to omniscience, and to the subtle obstacles to omniscience--if one meditates with that wisdom which grows from meditation and which sees directly the three degrees of the lack of a self-nature; this itself grows from following the practices of study and meditation to come to an understanding of these three. Given this statement, it is not the case that in our own position we believe--as do those who assert the existence of functional things which exist truly--that one can eliminate impurities that one asserts exist in truth. The citation rather is demonstrating the principal tenet of how our own system describes the process of eliminating the two obstacles; that is, that we eliminate impurities by meditating upon how these same impurities lack any true existence. ************ The next selection introduces, briefly, the concept of the three levels of deep practice that correlate to the three degrees of selflessness. It is taken from The "Cloud of Offerings, which Pleases the Wise, and Illuminates the True Thought of the Treatise known as the 'Ornament of Realizations,'" being a Combined Word Commentary and Dialectical Analysis of the Fifth Chapter of the Treatise, by Choney Lama Dra

rows.english: When we say that a craving spirit looks at a stream of water and sees pus and blood, by the way, we are only talking about some kinds of craving spirits, and not all of them. This is because there are many kinds of craving spirits: some with obstacles in the world around them that prevent them from relieving their craving; some with obstacles that are parts of their bodies; and some with obstacles that relate to the food or drink itself.

rows.wylie: der thal, chos kyi grags pa'i lung don ni, grangs can gyis rgyang ring thung gi gzugs la bltas pa de'i tshe na, rgyang ring thung gi gzugs dang , mig shes gnyis kyi bar du, las gzugs gsal mi gsal skye ba'i dbang gis, gzugs gsal bar snang mi snang 'jog pa yin gyi, gzugs kyi rnam pa shar ba'i sgo nas gzugs gsal bar snang mi snang 'jog pa ma yin zhes khas blangs pa la, de lta bu'i las gzugs gnyis po des rgyang ring thung gi gzugs gnyis po de bsgribs sam ma bsgribs, bsgribs na mig shes kyis gzugs gnyis po de ma mthong bar thal, des de sgrib pa'i phyir
rows.english: This is a fact, for the actual meaning of Master Dharmakirti's statement is as follows. The Numerist School is describing a situation where you are looking at a physical form either from far away, or from up close. They say that, depending on the distance between you and the object, another physical form which is the result of karma, and which stands between your visual consciousness and the original form, is either clear or not. This then determines whether the original form appears to you distinctly or not. It is not the case though, they say, that what determines whether the original form appears clearly or not is whether or not you have a clear impression of this form. In reply then Master Dharmakirti is asking the Numerists: Let's consider these two cases of some intermediate physical form that comes from karma. Do they, or do they not, function to obscure the two original forms, the one at a distance, and the other close by? If they were to obscure them, then your visual consciousness could never see the two original forms, since they would have been obscured by the others.

rows.acip: DE LTAR BYAS NA, ZAS SKOM NYID LA YOD PA'I SGRIB PA CAN GYI YI DVAGS KYIS LONGS SPYOD PA LA MA BRTZAMS KYI BAR DU BZA' BTUNG DNGOS YIN KYANG , DES LONGS SPYOD PAR BRTZAMS PA NA, ZAS DE'I RIGS 'DRA PHYI MA RNAG KHRAG TU SKYE BA YIN GYI, RNAG KHRAG TU SNANG BA'I SNANG BA TZAM GYIS BZA' BTUNG GI BYA BA BYED PA MA YIN TE, DE YIN NA LAS 'BRAS LA SKUR BA BTAB PAR 'GYUR BA'I PHYIR, DER THAL, DE LTA BU'I YI DVAGS KYIS LAS 'BRAS LA SKUR BA BTAB PAR 'GYUR BA'I PHYIR,
rows.wylie: de ltar byas na, zas skom nyid la yod pa'i sgrib pa can gyi yi dvags kyis longs spyod pa la ma brtsams kyi bar du bza' btung dngos yin kyang , des longs spyod par brtsams pa na, zas de'i rigs 'dra phyi ma rnag khrag tu skye ba yin gyi, rnag khrag tu snang ba'i snang ba tsam gyis bza' btung gi bya ba byed pa ma yin te, de yin na las 'bras la skur ba btab par 'gyur ba'i phyir, der thal, de lta bu'i yi dvags kyis las 'bras la skur ba btab par 'gyur ba'i phyir
rows.english: Given all this, consider craving spirits that have obstacles that relate to their food and drink itself. The food and drink there really is food and drink, until such time as the spirit starts trying to eat or drink it. When he does try to do so, then the continuum of the food into the next moment starts becoming pus and blood. It is not though that it is the simple appearance of something as pus and blood that could ever function as something to eat or drink. If this were the case, then the rules of karma and its consequences would have to be less than what they really are. And this is true, for if a craving spirit like this ever existed it would represent a failure of the laws of karma and its consequences.

rows.english: [3] Now the Levels of Listeners [by Master Asanga] says that, when you are practicing to purify the mind of the obstacles of sleepiness and fogginess, you should "press them upon each other." It also states that, when you are practicing to purify the mind of other kinds of obstacles, such as attraction to the objects of the senses, you should seat yourself upon a platform or smaller seat and assume the full lotus position. Therefore the third preliminary is to seat yourself on a comfortable cushion, sit up straight, and assume a full lotus position with your legs (a half lotus is also acceptable). In this pose then sink your mind deep into the thoughts of taking refuge, and the wish for enlightenment. 5 Visualizing the Garden

rows.english: [5] It is extremely difficult to bring the path to grow within the stream of your mind if all you practice is the various principal causes. You also need the supporting causes for the path to grow; you need to gather together the different factors that are conducive to the path, and you need to clean yourself of the factors that are obstacles, the ones that oppose the path. Therefore you must train your mind in the Seven Ingredients, which include in them all the critical points for gathering good and cleaning away obstacles. 7 Prostration

rows.acip: ,'DI LA SDUG BSNGAL GYI KHYAD PAR MDOR BSDU NA GSUM LAS LONGS SPYOD DAG LA PHYI'I SGRIB PA CAN NI CHU MIG DANG MTSE'U DANG CHU KLUNG LA SOGS PAR BZA' BA DANG , BTUNG BA DAG MTHONG ZHING DE DANG DER BRGYUG PA NA LAG NA RAL GRI DANG DBYUG PA LA SOGS PA THOGS PAS 'GOG PA DANG , CHU LA SOGS PA'ANG RNAG LA SOGS PAR MTHONG BAS SPYAD DU MED PA'O,
rows.wylie: 'di la sdug bsngal gyi khyad par mdor bsdu na gsum las longs spyod dag la phyi'i sgrib pa can ni chu mig dang mtshe'u dang chu klung la sogs par bza' ba dang , btung ba dag mthong zhing de dang der brgyug pa na lag na ral gri dang dbyug pa la sogs pa thogs pas 'gog pa dang , chu la sogs pa'ang rnag la sogs par mthong bas spyad du med pa'o
rows.english: The sufferings of these craving spirits can all be reduced to three different kinds. First are those with outer obstacles to what they need to live on. People like this approach a place like a mountain spring, or a pond or stream, and catch sight of something that they could eat or drink. They race ahead to get it, only to be forced back by beings cutting them with knives, or beating them with clubs and such. Or else they come to the side of some water and find themselves unable to drink of it, for then it looks to them like blood and pus or the like.

rows.english: Those craving spirits with inner obstacles have mouths no bigger than the eye of a needle, spouting with flame. Their throats are the size of a guitar string, but their bellies are huge. rows.english: His job is to inform beings who are headed for the hells, those who are ignorant of why they must go there, just what they did to deserve such a birth. He is attended by some thirty-six types of craving spirits. These spirits may, in general, be divided into three different groups: those with outer obstacles, those with inner obstacles, and those with obstacles in the very nature of what they try to eat or drink. Such spirits who live in the lands of men or pleasure beings have no particular place, and are found throughout these areas.

rows.english: The very same process then occurs, in respective order, with the inhabitants of the eastern continent and those of the continent to the west--Cattle Users. Thus the process for them is that they first take rebirth as pleasure beings of the desire realm.

rows.wylie: dol pa'i zhal nas kyang , zhar la tshogs gsog pa dang sgrib pa sbyong , lha dang bla ma la gsol ba 'debs shing rus shing dang bcas nas nan tan gyis bsams na, lo brgyar yang mi skye snyam pa zhig kyang 'dus byas so na mi sdod pas ci zhig ltar la skye ba yin gsung ngo
rows.english: Dolpa once stated, You must along the way undertake practices to amass the energy of good deeds, and to purify yourself of spiritual obstacles. So too you must make supplication to the angels, and to your Lama. If then you put all your heart into contemplating this attitude, if you focus on it, you will be able to attain it. Things produced by causes have a basic nature that they can never just stay the same, and you will find that you can arrive at certain kinds of attitudes that you thought you could never develop in a thousand years of trying.

rows.acip: ,DE NAS BYAMS PA DANG SNYING RJE'I RTZA BA CAN GYI BYANG CHUB KYI MCHOG TU SEMS BSKYED PA LA 'KHOR LO SGYUR BA'I RGYAL PO SPYAN 'DREN PA'I GNAS KHANG SOGS BYI DOR BYED PA BZHIN DU 'GAL RKYEN SGRIB PA BSHAGS PA DANG , MTHUN RKYEN TSOGS BSAGS NAS BYANG CHUB KYI SEMS GZUNG DGOS PA'I SNGA MA LE'U GNYIS PA DANG , PHYI MA LE'U GSUM PAS BSTAN TO,
rows.wylie: de nas byams pa dang snying rje'i rtsa ba can gyi byang chub kyi mchog tu sems bskyed pa la 'khor lo sgyur ba'i rgyal po spyan 'dren pa'i gnas khang sogs byi dor byed pa bzhin du 'gal rkyen sgrib pa bshags pa dang , mthun rkyen tshogs bsags nas byang chub kyi sems gzung dgos pa'i snga ma le'u gnyis pa dang , phyi ma le'u gsum pas bstan to
rows.english: You must go about developing the wish to achieve supreme enlightenment, that wish whose very root is love and compassion, in the same way that you would go about preparing to welcome a King who ruled the entire world by cleaning your house, and so on. You will be able to acquire this wish by purifying all of the factors which obstruct your spiritual realizations, and gathering together the power of good deeds which promote them. These two subjects are covered respectively in the second and third chapters.

rows.english: Emptiness is the antidote For the darkness of the obstacles Of affliction and to omniscience. How could it be that those Who hope for omniscience quickly Would neglect meditating upon it?

rows.acip: ,NYON MONGS PA'I SGRIB PA DANG SHES BYA'I SGRIB PA'I MUN PA'I GNYEN PO YANG STONG PA NYID RTOGS PA'I SHES RAB YIN PAS MYUR DU SGRIB GNYIS ZAD PA'I THAMS CAD MKHYEN PA 'DOD PAS STONG NYID DE NI JI LTAR SGOM PAR MI BYED DE DE DANG BRAL NA NYON SGRIB KYI SA BON YANG SPONG MI NUS SO,
rows.wylie: nyon mongs pa'i sgrib pa dang shes bya'i sgrib pa'i mun pa'i gnyen po yang stong pa nyid rtogs pa'i shes rab yin pas myur du sgrib gnyis zad pa'i thams cad mkhyen pa 'dod pas stong nyid de ni ji ltar sgom par mi byed de de dang bral na nyon sgrib kyi sa bon yang spong mi nus so
rows.english: The wisdom which realizes emptiness is, moreover, the antidote for the darkness of both the mental-affliction obstacles and the obstacles to knowledge. How could it ever be then that--if you hoped to achieve quickly the state of omniscience, the state where you end finally both the obstacles--you would neglect to go and meditate upon emptiness? Without this, you would never be able to eliminate even the seeds of the mental-affliction obstacles.

rows.wylie: gzhan dbang ni don dam pa'i ngo bo nyid du med pas don dam pa ngo bo nyid med pa zhes bya ste, don dam pa ni gang la dmigs nas goms na sgrib pa zad par 'gyur ba yin na gzhan dbang la dmigs nas goms pas sgrib pa dag par byed mi nus pa'i phyir ro,
rows.english: It is because dependent things do not exist as things which have any nature of being ultimate that we can speak of that which does not have any nature of being ultimate. The point here is that "ultimate" refers to anything which, when you focus on and meditate upon it, your spiritual obstacles are brought to an end. Dependent things though cannot be described as such, since they do not have the power to help you purify yourself of your spiritual obstacles if you focus on and meditate upon them.

rows.english: Why is this the case? Suppose that a person came to an understanding that they could purify themselves of their spiritual obstacles by focussing on, and then meditating upon, the fact that dependent things are empty of [certain] constructs. It is possible then that they might entertain the thought that--because to go through this process they had to focus upon dependent things as an example--then these same dependent things would be objects of [the path of] total purity. This in turn would mean that these dependent things were ultimate. A person would not though entertain this same thought about constructs.

rows.acip: 'O NA RANG LUGS LA SGRIB GNYIS KYI DRI MA SPONG TSUL JI LTAR BYED SNYAM NA, BDAG MED PHRA RAGS GSUM RIM PA BZHIN DU THOS BSAM GYIS GTAN LA PHAB NAS SGOM BYUNG GIS BSGOMS PAS MNGON SUM DU MTHONG BA NA NYON MONGS PA'I SGRIB PA DANG , SHES SGRIB RAGS PA DANG , SHES SGRIB PHRA MO GSUM RTZA BA NAS ZAD PAR BYED NUS ZHES STON PA YIN PAS, DNGOS SMRA BA 'DOD PA LTAR DRI MA BDEN GRUB KHAS BLANGS NAS SPONG BA MIN GYI, DRI MA BDEN MED BSGOMS NAS DRI MA SPONG BA YIN NO ZHES RANG LUGS KYI SGRIB GNYIS SPONG TSUL GTZO BOR STON PA YIN,
rows.wylie: 'o na rang lugs la sgrib gnyis kyi dri ma spong tshul ji ltar byed snyam na, bdag med phra rags gsum rim pa bzhin du thos bsam gyis gtan la phab nas sgom byung gis bsgoms pas mngon sum du mthong ba na nyon mongs pa'i sgrib pa dang , shes sgrib rags pa dang , shes sgrib phra mo gsum rtsa ba nas zad par byed nus zhes ston pa yin pas, dngos smra ba 'dod pa ltar dri ma bden grub khas blangs nas spong ba min gyi, dri ma bden med bsgoms nas dri ma spong ba yin no zhes rang lugs kyi sgrib gnyis spong tshul gtso bor ston pa yin
rows.english: "Well then," you may think to yourself, "how do we in our own position describe the process by which one eliminates the various impurities?" It has been taught that: One can gain the ability to put a total end to the three--that is, to the obstacles of the mental afflictions, to the gross obstacles to omniscience, and to the subtle obstacles to omniscience--if one meditates with that wisdom which grows from meditation and which sees directly the three degrees of the lack of a self-nature; this itself grows from following the practices of study and meditation to come to an understanding of these three. Given this statement, it is not the case that in our own position we believe--as do those who assert the existence of functional things which exist truly--that one can eliminate impurities that one asserts exist in truth. The citation rather is demonstrating the principal tenet of how our own system describes the process of eliminating the two obstacles; that is, that we eliminate impurities by meditating upon how these same impurities lack any true existence. ************ We turn next to comments on whether the lower degrees of selflessness are true emptiness; these are taken from "The Cloud of Offerings, which Pleases the Wise, and Illuminates the True Thought of the Treatise known as the 'Ornament of Realizations,'" being a Combined Word Commentary and Dialectical Analysis of the Fifth Chapter of the Treatise. This work was composed by Choney Lama Drakpa Shedrup (1675-1748),

rows.english: When we say that a craving spirit looks at a stream of water and sees pus and blood, by the way, we are only talking about some kinds of craving spirits, and not all of them. rows.english: And then it's just the same as where we learn to live on nothing more than a tiny pill made from the essence of some medicinal plant. Utilizing the path of habituation, we work our way gradually through the rest of the bodhisattva levels, transforming things with mere instants of absolute purity. At some point, we fulfill the goal characterized by eliminating each and every one of our obstacles. When we do reach this juncture, we say that this same state of wisdom, at the level of an Enlightened Being, is “focused upon final accomplishment of the goal.”

rows.english: Here is the first.  Now as far as spiritual obstacles, the Detailists do agree that there are two types; they call them “obstacles related to negative emotions” and “obstacles that do not relate to the negative emotions,” and in the latter case they sometimes also use the expression “spiritual darkness” for “obstacle.”  We don't see any explanation which says that they accept the expression “obstacles to omniscience.”

rows.english: Once a person though has been able to engender, within themselves, these experiences in their pure form, in the proper way, then the experiences continue on to higher and higher levels—more and more extraordinary—until they achieve a certain power. In the end, the adept who undertakes these deep practices is able to rid themselves, perfectly, of each and every obstacle to omniscience.

rows.english: And then the following syllogism expresses what's being stated here: Consider each and every knowable thing in the universe. The bodhisattva is indeed able, in the end, to rid themselves of each and every obstacle to the state of omniscience; Because they first learn the logical conversation which allows them to establish that nothing in the universe is real; and then through their formal meditation practice they gradually make this understanding into a personal, meditational realization: they develop, step by step, the path of the realized ones—the wisdom which no longer imagines that things are real. [Incidentally, Kedrup Je then goes on in his text to demonstrate how these four levels of deep practice are problematic in the lower schools which still assert that the functionality of things is innate to them—a group of schools which includes the present, Mind Only School!] Appendix E: Eight arguments on the existence of foundation consciousness There are eight famous arguments used to support the belief of the Mind Only School that a foundation consciousness does indeed exist.  They are presented by Je Tsongkapa in both the root text and autocommentary of his Difficult Points in the Mind Only School, and thus commented upon by The Blade in his Golden Key. We have added the Key to this translation project precisely because it does make it easier for all of us to then make the deep jump into Je Tsongkapa's much more difficult treatment.  On some points though this means a much

rows.english: Here is how The Light puts it: When we say “deceptive,” what we're referring to is the state of mind which focuses upon things which are, in fact, completely devoid of any essence of their own, and imputes them to have a nature which is the opposite. rows.wylie: 'dis sems can rnams dngos po ji ltar gnas pa'i rang bzhin lta ba la sgrib pa ste rmongs par byed pa'i phyir na gti mug ste, ma rig pa dngos po'i ngo bo rang bzhin gyis yod pa ma yin pa la, rang bzhin gyis yod par sgro 'dogs par byed pa yin lugs kyi rang bzhin mthong ba la sgrib pa'i bdag nyid can ni kun rdzob bo
rows.english: Dark ignorance is given its name from the fact that it leaves living beings in the dark: it draws a veil over our ability to see how things really exist—their nature. Misunderstanding enables us to see things as more than they actually are: it makes us believe that the essential nature of things—which is anything but these things' existing through some nature of their own—is for them to exist through just such a nature. “Deception” then is that entity whose nature is to veil our ability to see the true nature of things: the way they truly are.

rows.acip: DES GANG LA SGRIB NA YANG DAG KUN RDZOB 'DOD CES PAS YANG DAG PA'I DON LA SGRIB PAS KUN RDZOB BAM SGRIB BYED DU 'DOD CES PA STE, YANG LOG GNYIS KYI NANG NAS YANG DAG KUN RDZOB TU STON PA MIN NO,,
rows.wylie: des gang la sgrib na yang dag kun rdzob 'dod ces pas yang dag pa'i don la sgrib pas kun rdzob bam sgrib byed du 'dod ces pa ste, yang log gnyis kyi nang nas yang dag kun rdzob tu ston pa min no
rows.english: What is it that this reality veils? Given the wording “deceived about what is actually there,” what we're referring to is deception—a veil—in the sense of what covers & conceals actual reality. This is not meant to be a reference to a “correct” form of deceptive reality, in the division of that reality into correct & mistaken.

rows.acip: DE LTA NA MUN PAS RANG GIS RANG SGRIB PAR 'GYUR LA, DE 'DOD NA MUN KHUNG DU BUM PA MI MTHONG BA BZHIN DU, MUN PA YANG MI MTHONG BAR 'GYUR RO,,

rows.acip: ,GANG ZAG BDEN GRUB 'GOG PA'I RIGS PA'I RNAM GRANGS MTHA' YAS PA'I SHES RAB MI SKYED KYANG, NYON MONGS KYI SA BON GYI GNYEN PO RDZOGS PAR SGOM PA YOD LA, SHES BYA'I SGRIB PA'I GNYEN PO RDZOGS PAR SGOM PA NI MED DO,,
rows.wylie: gang zag bden grub 'gog pa'i rigs pa'i rnam grangs mtha' yas pa'i shes rab mi skyed kyang, nyon mongs kyi sa bon gyi gnyen po rdzogs par sgom pa yod la, shes bya'i sgrib pa'i gnyen po rdzogs par sgom pa ni med do
rows.english: It is not the case that these individuals are able to give rise to that wisdom where we used literally countless forms of reasoning to block the idea that the person could exist in some real way. Nonetheless, they do possess a practice where they are able to meditate, in full, upon the antidotes for the seeds of the negative emotions. At the same time, they do not possess a practice where they can meditate, in a complete way, upon the the antidotes to the obstacles to omniscience.

rows.english: The own quality for the eight freedoms is that they act to liberate us from impediments to balanced meditation.

rows.acip: RNAM PAR THAR PA BRGYAD NI NANG LA GZUGS CAN DU 'DU SHES PA MA BSHIG PAR PHYI ROL GYI GZUGS LA LTA BA DANG, NANG LA 'DU SHES DE BSHIG NAS PHYI ROL GYI GZUGS LA LTA BA'I RNAM THAR GNYIS NI, SPRUL PA LA GEGS BYED PA'I SGRIB PA'I GNYEN PO'O,,
rows.wylie: rnam par thar pa brgyad ni nang la gzugs can du 'du shes pa ma bshig par phyi rol gyi gzugs la lta ba dang, nang la 'du shes de bshig nas phyi rol gyi gzugs la lta ba'i rnam thar gnyis ni, sprul pa la gegs byed pa'i sgrib pa'i gnyen po'o
rows.english: Within the eight types of freedom, we have the freedom where we look at outer forms without having disassembled our conceiving of things possessed of form on the inside. And then we have the freedom where we look at outer forms after having disassembled this conception about the inside. These two types of freedom then act as antidotes for obstacles which block our ability to emanate ourselves.

rows.wylie: ji ltar te dper na bum pa dang 'khar gzhong la sogs pa'i snod kyi mi 'dra ba'i dbye ba du ma yod kyang, mi 'dra ba'i dbye ba de yis snod de dag tu gtogs pa ste der khyab pa'i nam mkha' la ni, sgrib pa thams cad bkag tsam du mtshungs pa'i phyir, de las gzhan pa'i dbye ba med pa
rows.english: Now there are many different types of vessels, such as a water pitcher or a bronze bowl. But let's consider what is contained in all those different kinds of vessels: the empty space that overarches them all. All these empty spaces are exactly the same, in the sense that each of them is the simple absence of physical obstruction. That is, there are no other distinctions to be made here.

rows.acip: BCOM LDAN 'DAS KYIS THUGS BRTZE BAR DGONGS TE, THOS NA CI NAS SEMS CAN THAMS CAD BLA NA MED PA YANG DAG PAR RDZOGS PA'I BYANG CHUB LAS SLAR MI LDOG PAR 'GYUR BA DANG, SDIG PA THAMS CAD DANG, LAS KYI SGRIB PA THAMS CAD YONGS SU BYANG ZHING YONGS SU BAS PAR 'GYUR BA DANG, BDUD SDIG CAN GYIS MI BRDZI BAR 'GYUR BA'I DE BZHIN GSHEGS PA DE DAG GI MTSAN DANG, SNGON GYI SMON LAM GYI KHYAD PAR RGYAS PA DANG, SANGS RGYAS KYI ZHING GI YON TAN BKOD PA'I GNAS RNAMS BSHAD DU GSOL,
rows.wylie: bcom ldan 'das kyis thugs brtse bar dgongs te, thos na ci nas sems can thams cad bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub las slar mi ldog par 'gyur ba dang, sdig pa thams cad dang, las kyi sgrib pa thams cad yongs su byang zhing yongs su bas par 'gyur ba dang, bdud sdig can gyis mi brdzi bar 'gyur ba'i de bzhin gshegs pa de dag gi mtshan dang, sngon gyi smon lam gyi khyad par rgyas pa dang, sangs rgyas kyi zhing gi yon tan bkod pa'i gnas rnams bshad du gsol
rows.english: O Conqueror, we ask that you look upon us with the love of your heart, and elucidate for us the holy names of certain Enlightened Beings Who Have Gone That Way; and the details of the prayers that they made in days gone by; and the wonders of the enlightened realms in which they dwell.  For we know that when any being in the universe hears these things, they become unstoppable in their own journey to the state of matchless and total Buddhahood.  When they hear these things, they are completely cleaned of each and every bad deed they have ever done—each one of these actions comes to an utter end.

rows.english: May all these beings, by my mystic power, catch at some point the sound of my name; and later may they recall this name, and speak it.  And thus may they be cleaned, completely, of all their karmic obstacles from the past.  May that lifetime in the cycle of pain then be their last.

rows.english: O Conqueror, we ask you to elucidate for us the holy names of certain Enlightened Beings Who Have Gone That Way; and the details of the prayers that they made in days gone by. We ask you to do this so that living beings may be completely cleaned of each and every bad deed they have ever done; and in order to guide those beings who will come later, in those future days when false versions of your holy teachings may have spread in the world. Atha Bhagavan Manjushriye Kumarabhutaya sadhukaram adat.

Therefore the third preliminary is to seat yourself on a comfortable cushion, sit up straight, and assume a full lotus position with your legs (a half lotus is also acceptable). rows.wylie: de nas lam rgyud la skye ba'i mthun rkyen tshogs bsag pa dang 'gal rkyen sgrib pa sbyong, ba'i lhan cig byed rkyen med na nyer len gyi rgyu dmigs rnam skyong ba tsam la 'bad kyang lam shin tu skye dka' bas bsag sbyang gi gnad rnams bsdus pa'i yan lag bdun pas rgyud sbyang dgos so de la
rows.english: It is extremely difficult to bring the path to grow within the stream of your mind if all you practice is the various principal causes. You also need the supporting causes for the path to grow; you need to gather together the different factors that are conducive to the path, and you need to clean yourself of the factors that are obstacles, the ones that oppose the path. Therefore you must train your mind in the Seven Ingredients, which include in them all the critical points for gathering good and cleaning away obstacles.

rows.wylie: bsngo ba'i yan lag ni phyag 'tshal ba dang zhes pa'i tshigs bcad de gong gi yan, lag drug gi dge bas mtshon nas dge rtsa thams cad sems can thams cad dang thun mong du byas te rdzogs pa'i byang chub kyi rgyur 'dun pa drag pos bsngos pas nam yang mi 'dzad pa'o de ltar tshig de dag gi don go bar byas la yid gzhan du ma yengs par dal bus ji skad bstan pa bzhin du byas na bsod nams kyi phung po dpag tu med pa 'dzin to de ltar na phyag dang mchod pa dang bskul ba dang gsol ba gdab pa dang yi rang dang lnga ni mthun rkyen tshogs gsog pa yin la bshags pa ni 'gal rkyen sgrib pa sbyong ba dang yi rang gi phyogs gcig rang gi dge ba byas pa la dga' ba bsgom pa ni rang gi dge ba spel bar yang 'gyur ro bsngo bas ni bsags pa dang sbyangs pa dang spel ba'i dge ba rnams nyung ngu'ang ches mang bar spel ba dang gnas skabs su 'bras bu phyung ste zad par 'gyur ba rnams kyang nam yang mi zad par byed pa ste bsdu na bsag pa dang sbyang ba dang spel zhing mi zad par byed pa gsum du 'du'o
rows.english: The Six Preliminaries and the Seven Ingredients The seventh ingredient is dedication, which is found in the verse with the words "prostrations and..." [The full verse reads: I dedicate To my future enlightenment All my merit, Whatever little goodness I may have gathered here By bowing myself and offering, By confessing and rejoicing, By urging and supplication.] Here we are taking all the virtuous seeds within us, represented by the goodness we have accomplished in practicing the six ingredients that have already come, and dedicating them as a cause for the full enlightenment of ourselves and every living being, together. Make this dedication with tremendous will, and the power of your good will flow forever, and never Read this prayer as I have taught you to here; understand what each verse means, and say it out slowly, without letting your mind wander to something else. If you can do this, then you will gain a great mountain of good deeds, beyond any kind of measuring. Five of the ingredients we have listed here—prostrating, offering, urging, supplicating, and rejoicing—help you to gather together the different factors that are conducive to the path. One of them, confessing, helps you clean yourself of the factors that are obstacles, ones that oppose the path. One part of rejoicing—dwelling in a sense of gladness over the good you have done yourself—also functions to multiply your virtue. Dedication works to multiply, fantastically, even the minor good deeds you have done in the acts of gathering, and cleaning, and multiplying. It also takes good deeds that are short-term, those that are going to give a good result and then disappear, and changes them so that they will never be exhausted. In brief, it functions in all three ways: to gather, to clean, and to multiply such that goodness never ends.

rows.acip: DOL PA'I ZHAL NAS KYANG ZHAR LA TSOGS GSOG, PA DANG SGRIB PA SBYONG LHA DANG BLA MA LA GSOL BA 'DEBS SHING RUS SHING DANG BCAS NAS NAN TAN GYIS BSAMS NA LO BRGYAR YANG MI SKYE SNYAM PA ZHIG KYANG 'DUS BYAS SO NA MI SDOD PAS CI ZHIG LTAR LA SKYE BA YIN GSUNG NGO
rows.wylie: dol pa'i zhal nas kyang zhar la tshogs gsog, pa dang sgrib pa sbyong lha dang bla ma la gsol ba 'debs shing rus shing dang bcas nas nan tan gyis bsams na lo brgyar yang mi skye snyam pa zhig kyang 'dus byas so na mi sdod pas ci zhig ltar la skye ba yin gsung ngo
rows.english: Dolpa once stated, You must alongthe way undertake practices to amass the energy of good deeds, and to purify yourself of spiritual obstacles. So too you must make supplication to the angels, and to your Lama. If then you put all your heart if you focus on it, then you will be able to attain it. Things produced by causes have a basic nature that they can never just stay the same, and you will find that you can arrive at certain kinds of attitudes that you thought you could never develop in a century.

rows.acip: CHOS BZHI BSTAN PA'I MDO LAS STOBS BZHI DANG LDAN NA BYAS SHING BSAGS PA'I, SDIG PA THAMS CAD 'DAG PAR GSUNGS PAS LAS KYI SGRIB PA SBYANG BAR 'DOD PAS NI GNYEN PO STOBS BZHI LA 'BAD PAR BYA'O
rows.wylie: chos bzhi bstan pa'i mdo las stobs bzhi dang ldan na byas shing bsags pa'i, sdig pa thams cad 'dag par gsungs pas las kyi sgrib pa sbyang bar 'dod pas ni gnyen po stobs bzhi la 'bad par bya'o
rows.english: The Sutra on the Four Practices states that, if a person keeps the four practices, then they can purify themselves of every bad deed which they may have committed and collected. Thus we can say that, if you hope to clean yourself of the spiritual obstacles created by your past bad deeds, you should make great efforts in the four antidote powers.

rows.acip: DE'I PHYIR SEMS BSKYED PA 'DI NI LAS KYI SGRIB PA THAMS CAD RNAM PAR SBYONG BAR BYED DE, JI SKAD DU GSUNGS PA BYANG CHUB SEMS DPA' DE GAL TE SNGA DRO LTUNG BA BYUNG NA NYI MA PHYED NA BYANG CHUB KYI SEMS MNGON DU BYED PA DE'I TSUL KHRIMS KYI PHUNG PO MTHA' MED PA NYID DU RIG PAR BYA'O DE BZHIN DU RIGS KYI BU BSKAL PA'I ME DANG MNYAM PA'I BYANG CHUB KYIS SEMS NI NYES PAR SPYOD PA THAMS CAD SREG PAR BYED DO ZHES RGYA CHER RO
rows.wylie: de'i phyir sems bskyed pa 'di ni las kyi sgrib pa thams cad rnam par sbyong bar byed de, ji skad du gsungs pa byang chub sems dpa' de gal te snga dro ltung ba byung na nyi ma phyed na byang chub kyi sems mngon du byed pa de'i tshul khrims kyi phung po mtha' med pa nyid du rig par bya'o de bzhin du rigs kyi bu bskal pa'i me dang mnyam pa'i byang chub kyis sems ni nyes par spyod pa thams cad sreg par byed do zhes rgya cher ro
rows.english: And so we can say that anyone who is able to develop this particular version of the wish is able to clean from themselves, completely, each and every obstacle caused by their past bad deeds. This is the point of the scripture that states: Suppose any particular bodhisattva commits a transgression of their vows in the morning, but by noon has had a true feeling of the Wish for enlightenment. You should understand that they have created nothing but immeasurable mountains of pure conduct by spending their day this way. Again and again too we see statements then like "This Wish for enlightenment, o child of noble family, is equal in its strength to the fire that ends the world; it annihilates each and every bad deed you've ever done."

rows.acip: DE BZHIN DU 'PHAGS PA BYAMS PA'I RNAM PAR THAR PAR RIGS KYI BU 'DI LTA STE SGRON ME, GCIG KHYIM MAM GNAS KHANG CI 'DRA BA CIG TU RAB TU BCUG NA DE RAB TU BCUG MA THAG TU LO STONG DU BSAGS PA'I MUN PA MUN NAG KYANG SEL ZHING SNANG BAR BYED DO DE BZHIN DU THAMS CAD MKHYEN PAR SEMS BSKYED PA'I SGRON ME GCIG SEMS CAN GYI BSAM PA'I THIBS PO MA RIG PA'I MUN PA DANG LDAN PA CI 'DRA CIG TU RAB TU ZHUGS NA DE RAB TU ZHUGS MA THAG TU BRJOD DU MED PA'I BSKAL PA BRGYA STONG PHRAG TU BSAGS PA'I LAS DANG NYON MONGS PA'I SGRIB PA'I MUN PA MUN NAG KYANG SEL ZHING YE SHES KYI SNANG BA, YANG DAG PAR BSKYED DO ZHES SO
rows.wylie: de bzhin du 'phags pa byams pa'i rnam par thar par rigs kyi bu 'di lta ste sgron me, gcig khyim mam gnas khang ci 'dra ba cig tu rab tu bcug na de rab tu bcug ma thag tu lo stong du bsags pa'i mun pa mun nag kyang sel zhing snang bar byed do de bzhin du thams cad mkhyen par sems bskyed pa'i sgron me gcig sems can gyi bsam pa'i thibs po ma rig pa'i mun pa dang ldan pa ci 'dra cig tu rab tu zhugs na de rab tu zhugs ma thag tu brjod du med pa'i bskal pa brgya stong phrag tu bsags pa'i las dang nyon mongs pa'i sgrib pa'i mun pa mun nag kyang sel zhing ye shes kyi snang ba, yang dag par bskyed do zhes so
rows.english: In this same vein, The Biography of Loving One says: It's like this, o child of noble family. Think of a single butter lamp; you can carry it into any cottage or house at all and it will clear away the dark and light up the place, the minute you step in, even if the dark has been accumulating there for the last thousand years. Now think of the Wish to reach total omniscience, just a single lamp of the Wish. Suppose you stick it for a moment into the mind of any particular living being smothered in the darkness of ignorance. In the very next moment, all the darkness of the spiritual obstacles created by karma and the mental afflictions—darkness that has been collecting there for so many millions of eons that words could not express their number—is cleared away; and the light of wisdom is born in its fullness.

And why is that? rows.acip: LAS KYI SGRIB PA RNAM PAR DAG PA LAS KYANG BYANG CHUB SEMS DPA' LTUNG BA LA LTUNG, BA MA YIN PAR MTHONG BA DANG 'DUL BA MA YIN PA LA 'DUL BAR MTHONG BA DANG KUN NAS NYON MONGS PA LA RNAM PAR BYANG BAR MTHONG BA DANG 'KHOR BA'I KHAMS LA MYA NGAN LAS 'DAS PA'I DBYINGS SU MTHONG BA DES LAS KYI SGRIB PA RNAM PAR DAG PA 'THOB BO ZHES GSUNG SO
rows.wylie: las kyi sgrib pa rnam par dag pa las kyang byang chub sems dpa' ltung ba la ltung, ba ma yin par mthong ba dang 'dul ba ma yin pa la 'dul bar mthong ba dang kun nas nyon mongs pa la rnam par byang bar mthong ba dang 'khor ba'i khams la mya ngan las 'das pa'i dbyings su mthong ba des las kyi sgrib pa rnam par dag pa 'thob bo zhes gsung so
rows.english: The sutra called Purifying Yourself of the Spiritual Obstacles Created by Your Past Deeds also says: Think of those bodhisattvas who see that a transgression of the vows is no transgression of the vows; who see that a failure to control yourself is to control yourself; who see that to be filled with mental affliction is to be totally pure; who see that the realm of the circle of suffering is the ultimate sphere of nirvana. It is these who succeed in purifying themselves of the spiritual obstacles created by their past deeds. [The point here of course is the recognition by these high beings that the ultimate nature even of opposites is the same, pure emptiness; not that—as some Tibetan schools have very wrongly taught—suffering and nirvana are somehow the same thing.]

rows.acip: SA'I SNYING PO'I MDO LAS SROG GCOD PA SPONG BA NI SEMS CAN THAMS CAD LA MI, 'JIGS PA SBYIN PA STE DGE BA'I LAS DES SNGON GYI MTHA' NAS 'KHOR BA'I CHU BOS KHYER TE SROG GCOD PA'I LAS KYI SGRIB PA DANG NYON MONGS PA'I SGRIB PA DANG CHOS KYI SGRIB PA BYAS PA DANG BYED DU BCUG PA DANG RJES SU YI RANG BA THAMS CAD 'JOMS TE MA LUS PAR ZAD PAR BYED DO
rows.wylie: sa'i snying po'i mdo las srog gcod pa spong ba ni sems can thams cad la mi, 'jigs pa sbyin pa ste dge ba'i las des sngon gyi mtha' nas 'khor ba'i chu bos khyer te srog gcod pa'i las kyi sgrib pa dang nyon mongs pa'i sgrib pa dang chos kyi sgrib pa byas pa dang byed du bcug pa dang rjes su yi rang ba thams cad 'joms te ma lus par zad par byed do
rows.english: As The Sutra of Kshitigarbha says, To give up the act of taking life is to make the gift of freedom from fear to every living being. And this virtuous karma destroys all the obstacles from the act of killing that you've carried in your mind for the beginningless time that you've been swept along in the river of suffering life. These are the obstacles of the karma of killing, the obstacles of the mental afflictions, and the obstacles to seeing all objects: obstacles that have come from either committing killing yourself, or getting others to kill for you, or rejoicing in how others have killed. And in this way every one of these obstacles is finished.

rows.english: Thus it is correct when [The Diamond Cutter] says that these forms of practice can clean you of every karmic obstacle, even those which are committed and collected. Resolving Some Sticky Issues about Purification There are a number of classic "sticky issues" about the concept of purification that appear throughout Buddhist literature over the centuries. Here is a brief presentation of some of the major issues which clarifies them briefly but fully; all the more an amazing feat since the author has done so in eloquent poetry. This selection is taken from "An Easy Path to Omniscience," being Advice, Set in Verses, on the Steps of the Path to Enlightenment, which was written by a former life of Pabongka Rinpoche: the first Changkya Rinpoche, Ngawang Lobsang Chunden (1642-1714).

rows.english: The Sutra on the Complete Purification of Every Karmic Obstacle includes that line about "If there comes a situation where they all assemble, and the the time is ripe..." rows.acip: 'DI NI GNAS MA YIN ZHING SKABS MED DE JI SRID SKRA'I RTZE MOS GZUGS PA'I TSAD, KYIS BSTAN PA TZAM GYIS MI DGE BA'I RTZA BA DANG LDAN PAR GYUR PA'I BYANG CHUB SEMS DPA' YANG BYANG CHUB KYI SHING DRUNG DU 'DUG PA NI GNAS MA YIN PAR SHES TE DGE BA'I CHOS THAMS CAD DANG LDAN PAR GYUR PA'I DE BZHIN GSHEGS PA MI DGE BA THAMS CAD SPANGS PAR GYUR PA BAG CHAGS KYI MTSAMS SBYOR BA DANG BCAS PA YANG SPANGS PA'I DE BZHIN GSHEGS PA LA LAS KYI SGRIB PA'I SKYON LTA 'BYUNG BAR GA LA 'GYUR
rows.wylie: 'di ni gnas ma yin zhing skabs med de ji srid skra'i rtse mos gzugs pa'i tshad, kyis bstan pa tsam gyis mi dge ba'i rtsa ba dang ldan par gyur pa'i byang chub sems dpa' yang byang chub kyi shing drung du 'dug pa ni gnas ma yin par shes te dge ba'i chos thams cad dang ldan par gyur pa'i de bzhin gshegs pa mi dge ba thams cad spangs par gyur pa bag chags kyi mtshams sbyor ba dang bcas pa yang spangs pa'i de bzhin gshegs pa la las kyi sgrib pa'i skyon lta 'byung bar ga la 'gyur
rows.english: In actuality, all these things are completely beyond the realm of possibility; there is no chance that they could have really happened. They had about as much reality as a sketch done with a single hair; you have to realize that this pose of being a bodhisattva with roots of non-virtue and then sitting under the tree there was a total impossibility. A being Gone Thus, one who possesses each and every virtuous quality, has eliminated each and every non-virtue; so too have they eliminated the very trace of even the seeds for negativity. How on earth then could One Thus Gone ever have any problem with some karmic obstacle?

rows.acip: 'DI LTAR LEGS PAR BSLABS PA'I SMAN PA BDAG NYID LA NAD MED BZHIN DU YANG NA, BLTAR BSTAN NAS SMAN KHAB DANG TSA BA DAG BSTEN PAR BYAS PAS DE'I RJES SU SLOB PA'I NAD PA DAG YONGS SU SOS PAR BYED PA DE BZHIN DU DE BZHIN GSHEGS PA SMAN PA'I RGYAL PO GNOD PA THAMS CAD ZHI BAR MDZAD PAS KYANG SGRIB PA MI MNGA' NA YANG NGA'I LAS 'DI'O RNAM PAR SMIN PA NI 'DI 'O ZHES PHRIN LAS STON PAR MDZAD DE
rows.wylie: 'di ltar legs par bslabs pa'i sman pa bdag nyid la nad med bzhin du yang na, bltar bstan nas sman khab dang tsha ba dag bsten par byas pas de'i rjes su slob pa'i nad pa dag yongs su sos par byed pa de bzhin du de bzhin gshegs pa sman pa'i rgyal po gnod pa thams cad zhi bar mdzad pas kyang sgrib pa mi mnga' na yang nga'i las 'di'o rnam par smin pa ni 'di 'o zhes phrin las ston par mdzad de
rows.english: Think of a very well-trained physician; he may not have any kind of illness himself, but still he might let his own blood, or stick himself with a medicine needle, or apply hot steel to himself, just so his students, the sick ones who are following him, will allow him to use these same methods to cure them. The One Gone Thus, the king of all physicians, is the same. Despite the fact that he has put a stop to every harm he himself could ever undergo, and so has no possible obstacle at all, he nonetheless undertakes as one of his enlightened acts to pretend, and to say "this is my karma," and "this is my karma ripening."

rows.english: When we say that a craving spirit looks at a stream of water and sees pus and blood, by the way, we are only talking about some kinds of craving spirits, and not all of them. rows.english: This is a fact, for the actual meaning of Master Dharmakirti's statement is as follows. The Numerist School is describing a situation where you are looking at a physical form either from far away, or from up close. They say that, depending on the distance between you and the object, another physical form which is the result of karma, and which stands between your visual consciousness and the original form, is either clear or not. This then determines whether the original form appears to you distinctly or not. It is not the case though, they say, that what determines whether the original form appears clearly or not is whether or not you have a clear impression of this In reply then Master Dharmakirti is asking the Numerists: Let's consider these two cases of some intermediate physical form that comes from karma. Do they, or do they not, function to obscure the two original forms, the one at a distance, and the other close by? If they were to obscure them, then your visual consciousness could never see the two original forms, since they would have been obscured by the others.

rows.acip: 'O NA RANG LUGS LA SGRIB GNYIS KYI DRI MA SPONG TSUL JI LTAR BYED SNYAM NA BDAG MED, PHRA RAGS GSUM RIM PA BZHIN DU THOS BSAM GYIS GTAN LA PHAB NAS SGOM BYUNG GIS BSGOMS PAS MNGON SUM DU MTHONG BA NA NYON MONGS PA'I SGRIB PA DANG SHES SGRIB, RAGS PA DANG SHES SGRIB PHRA MO GSUM RTZA BA NAS ZAD PAR BYED NUS ZHES STON PA YIN, PAS DNGOS SMRA BA 'DOD PA LTAR DRI MA BDEN GRUB KHAS BLANGS NAS SPONG BA MIN GYI DRI MA BDEN MED BSGOMS NAS DRI MA SPONG BA YIN NO ZHES RANG LUGS KYI SGRIB GNYIS SPONG TSUL GTZO BOR STON PA YIN
rows.wylie: 'o na rang lugs la sgrib gnyis kyi dri ma spong tshul ji ltar byed snyam na bdag med, phra rags gsum rim pa bzhin du thos bsam gyis gtan la phab nas sgom byung gis bsgoms pas mngon sum du mthong ba na nyon mongs pa'i sgrib pa dang shes sgrib, rags pa dang shes sgrib phra mo gsum rtsa ba nas zad par byed nus zhes ston pa yin, pas dngos smra ba 'dod pa ltar dri ma bden grub khas blangs nas spong ba min gyi dri ma bden med bsgoms nas dri ma spong ba yin no zhes rang lugs kyi sgrib gnyis spong tshul gtso bor ston pa yin
rows.english: "Well then," you may think to yourself, "how do we in our own position describe the process by which one eliminates the various impurities?" It has been taught that: One can gain the ability toput a total end tothe three—that is, to the obstacles of the mental afflictions, to the gross obstacles to omniscience, and to the subtle obstacles to omniscience—if one meditates with that wisdom which grows from meditation and which sees directly the three degrees of the lack of a self-nature; this itself grows from following the practices of study and meditation to come to an understanding of these three. Given this statement, it is not the case that in our own position we believe—as do those who assert the existence of functional things which exist truly—that one can eliminate impurities that one asserts exist in truth. The citation rather is demonstrating the principal tenet of how our own system describes the process of eliminating the two obstacles; that is, that we eliminate impurities by meditating upon how these same impurities lack any true existence. The next selection introduces, briefly, the concept of the three levels of deep practice that correlate to the three degrees of selflessness. It is taken from The "Cloud of Offerings, which Pleases the Wise, and Illuminates the True Thought of the Treatise known as the 'Ornament of Realizations,'" being a Combined Word Commentary and Dialectical Analysis of the Fifth Chapter of the Treatise, by Choney Lama Drakpa Shedrup (1675-1748), also an illustrious author of textbooks for Sera Mey Tibetan Monastery (ACIP electronic text S0195, Part Five, ff. 11b-12a).

rows.english: This part is explained by the Lord of the Teachings, Rongtikpa, and by Gung-ru Gyeltsen Sangpo in the following way: If we come to a realization of this object, emptiness, and then get used to what we have realized, then we no longer possess in our minds the obstacle of believing that things are real. And then because of this, we no longer have any fear about this thing—this emptiness. We go beyond all wrong ways of thinking—beyond all belief in things as real—and then we reach the ultimate end of the process of nirvana: meaning that we attain the level of a Buddha.

rows.acip: ZHES GSUNGS PA LTAR THABS DANG SHES RAB DBYER MED PAR SBYOR BA'I RDO RJE SEMS DPA'I RNAL 'BYOR NI RDO RJE STE THEG PA YANG DE'O, ,DE LA 'DIS 'GRO BA RGYU'I THEG PA DANG 'DIR 'GRO BA 'BRAS BU'I THEG PA GNYIS SO, ,THEG PA DES 'GRO BA'I SNGAGS KYI SDOM LDAN RNAMS LA BCAS PA'I BCAS PA DANG 'GAL BA'I LAS KYI SGRIB PA NI GNAS 'OG MAR 'KHRID PA DANG , YON TAN GONG MA SKYE BA LA SGRIB PAS NA LTUNG BA YIN LA,
rows.wylie: zhes gsungs pa ltar thabs dang shes rab dbyer med par sbyor ba'i rdo rje sems dpa'i rnal 'byor ni rdo rje ste theg pa yang de'o, ,de la 'dis 'gro ba rgyu'i theg pa dang 'dir 'gro ba 'bras bu'i theg pa gnyis so, ,theg pa des 'gro ba'i sngags kyi sdom ldan rnams la bcas pa'i bcas pa dang 'gal ba'i las kyi sgrib pa ni gnas 'og mar 'khrid pa dang , yon tan gong ma skye ba la sgrib pas na ltung ba yin la
rows.english: What Shantipa is describing here is that the yoga of the Warrior of Diamond is where we yoke together, indivisibly, method and wisdom.  This then is both the diamond and the way. This diamond way is both a way which is a cause--that is, a way by which we make our spiritual journey; and a way which is a result--the place to which we are journeying. Now when those who are traveling upon this way--that is, those who possess the vows of the secret word--act against the rules that have been set down for them, then this creates a karmic obstacle.  This obstacle leads them to a lower place, and obstructs them from developing higher spiritual qualities.  As such, it is called a "downfall."

rows.english: Chilupa's commentary to the Secret Collection says too that "They are completely indivisible."   What this is saying is that the paradise body of the being known as the Diamond Mind of Enlightenment arises from his Dharma body.  We live though in times where we are unable even to lay eyes upon the bodies of emanation in which these other bodies reside. And so the Enlightened Ones come and stay in the body of our Master, so that they can help others purify themselves of their karmic obstacles, and other such problems. The point is that in times like the present day, when people are unable to see a Buddha in the flesh, then the Enlightened Ones come and enter into the body of our Diamond Master, and thus perform Their deeds of benefit for every living being. ***

rows.acip: RKANG PA DANG PO GNYIS NI SMON 'JUG GNYIS KYI DON BSDU DANG , DE NAS GNYIS NI SDOM PA LNGA'I DON BSDU'O, ,MA GROL PA NI GTI MUG SOGS SGRIB PA GNYIS KYI 'CHING BAS BCINGS PA'I TSANGS PA LA SOGS PA STE DE RNAMS DGROL BA DANG NYAN RANG SHES SGRIB LAS MA BRGAL BA RNAMS DE LAS BSGRAL BA DANG , DMYAL BA LA SOGS PA DBUGS MA PHYIN PA RNAMS DBUGS DBYUNG ZHING SEMS CAN KUN MI GNAS PA'I MYA NGAN LAS 'DAS PA LA DGOD DO ZHES PA NI MAN SNYE DANG RDO RJE MKHA' 'GRO'I RNAM BSHAD GNYIS KA'I DGONGS PA'O, ,TSIGS BCAD THA MA 'DI 'JUG SEMS BSKYED PA LA MAN SNYER BSHAD DO,
rows.wylie: rkang pa dang po gnyis ni smon 'jug gnyis kyi don bsdu dang , de nas gnyis ni sdom pa lnga'i don bsdu'o, ,ma grol pa ni gti mug sogs sgrib pa gnyis kyi 'ching bas bcings pa'i tshangs pa la sogs pa ste de rnams dgrol ba dang nyan rang shes sgrib las ma brgal ba rnams de las bsgral ba dang , dmyal ba la sogs pa dbugs ma phyin pa rnams dbugs dbyung zhing sems can kun mi gnas pa'i mya ngan las 'das pa la dgod do zhes pa ni man snye dang rdo rje mkha' 'gro'i rnam bshad gnyis ka'i dgongs pa'o, ,tshigs bcad tha ma 'di 'jug sems bskyed pa la man snyer bshad do
rows.english: The first four lines [in the English] here summarize the meaning of the Wish for enlightenment, in both the form of a prayer, and action.  The next two lines summarize the five vows. The words "those who have yet to be freed" refer to beings such as the Pure One, Brahma, who are still bound in the fetters of ignorance and so on: the two kinds of obstacles; and we commit to free them. "Those who have yet to be saved" refers to those of the ways of listeners and self-made Buddhas, who are yet to be saved from the obstacles to omniscience; we commit to save them. "Those who have no comfort" is a reference to beings such as those in the realms of hell; we are resolving to bring them comfort.  And we decide finally to deliver all living beings to a state of nirvana which is beyond both of the extremes.  This is how both the Golden Harvest and the Explication of the Angel of Diamond both interpret these lines.  The Golden Harvest further explains the final verse as referring to the Wish for enlightenment in the form of action. ***

rows.wylie: da ltar rang res bla ma mi'i gzugs can du mthong ba yang dga' rab yin te, spyan snga blo rgyan gyis, ,rang re'i las ngan sgrib pa'i che tshod la, ,bla ma mi ru mthong ba'ang dga' tshad yin, ,khyi dang bong bur ma mthong bsod nams che, ,mos gus snying nas bskyed cig shAkya'i sras, ,zhes gsungs
rows.english: Even the fact that we can in our present condition see our Lama as a human being is quite an achievement.  As Chen-nga Lodru Gyeltsen once said, The fact that all of us, with the level Of bad deeds and obstacles that we have, Can even see our Lama as a human Is quite something of an achievement. It is our own great merit that we don't See Them as a dog, or a donkey. So feel love and reverence for Them, Deep from your hearts, Sons of the Shakya.

rows.acip: DE'I PHYIR TSOGS KYI ZHING 'GRAN ZLA MED PA BLA MA YIN PAS TSOGS GSOG PA BLA MA'I RNAL 'BYOR GYI SGO NAS BYED CING, SGRIB PA SBYANG BA RDOR SEMS BSGOM BZLAS KYI KHONGS SU 'DU GSUNGS,

rows.english: Therefore the one object that is unsurpassed for amassing virtue is your Lama; and this, said our Lama, is why we gather the collections of virtue through this practice of the Lama. rows.acip: BLA MA'I SPYI BO'I AOm LAS BDUD RTZI DKAR PO'I RGYUN BABS RANG GI SPYI BOR THIM, BUM PA'I DBANG THOB, LUS KYI SGRIB PA DAG ,LAM BSKYED RIM BSGOM PA LA DBANG, 'BRAS BU SPRUL SKU 'GRUB PA'I NUS PA BZHAG
rows.wylie: bla ma'i spyi bo'i aoM las bdud rtsi dkar po'i rgyun babs rang gi spyi bor thim, bum pa'i dbang thob, lus kyi sgrib pa dag ,lam bskyed rim bsgom pa la dbang, 'bras bu sprul sku 'grub pa'i nus pa bzhag
rows.english: From the letter om at the tips of the Lamas' heads comes forth a stream of white nectar.  It dissolves into the tip of your own head.  You receive the empowerment of the vase, and you are purified of all your physical obstacles.  You are empowered to practice the path of the stage of creation, and the ability to achieve one of your goals--the Emanation Body--is planted within you.

rows.acip: SUM CU RTZA GSUM DANG RGYAL CHEN RIGS BZHI'I LHA RNAMS LA DBANG PO GNYIS SBYOR GYI BDE BA YOD KYANG RLUNG 'DU 'PHROD KYI BDE BA TZAM LAS RTZA DANG KHAMS DKAR DMAR MED PAS DE'I BDE BA MED, YI DVAGS DANG DUD 'GRO LA DBANG PO GNYIS SBYOR GYI BDE BA YOD KYKANG LAS KYI SGRIB PA CHE ZHING DBANG PO RTUL BAS BDE BA LAM DU BYED MI NUS LA,
rows.wylie: sum cu rtsa gsum dang rgyal chen rigs bzhi'i lha rnams la dbang po gnyis sbyor gyi bde ba yod kyang rlung 'du 'phrod kyi bde ba tsam las rtsa dang khams dkar dmar med pas de'i bde ba med, yi dvags dang dud 'gro la dbang po gnyis sbyor gyi bde ba yod kykang las kyi sgrib pa che zhing dbang po rtul bas bde ba lam du byed mi nus la
rows.english: The gods of the Thirty-Three, and the Four Great Kings, do experience the bliss of joining the two organs, but as nothing more than the pleasure of the joining and mixing of the winds.  They do not get the experience of bliss that comes from channels, and the red and white elements, because they do not possess any of these inner parts.  Craving spirits and animals do possess the pleasure of union of the organs, but they have very bad obstacles caused by their past karma and are spiritually very stupid, and thus they are incapable of making this bliss a path.

rows.acip: 'KHOR LO SNGA MA LTAR NA PHYI NANG GNYIS KYI RTZIBS BCU DRUG ,RANG LUGS THUN MONG MIN PAR 'KHOR LO'I RTZIBS BRGYAD DANG NOR BU'I GZHOGS KHA BRGYAD BSDOMS PAS BCU DRUG ,RDO RJE NAG PO'I PHRENG BA PHYI NANG GNYIS BSDOMS PA BCU DRUG STE KHYON SUM CU SO GNYIS KYIS SPYI BO'I RTZA 'DAB SUM CU SO GNYIS MTSON, 'KHOR LOS DBU SKRA MI SGRIB PA DANG, DBU SKRAS 'KHOR LO MI SGRIB PAR BSGOM DGOS,
rows.wylie: 'khor lo snga ma ltar na phyi nang gnyis kyi rtsibs bcu drug ,rang lugs thun mong min par 'khor lo'i rtsibs brgyad dang nor bu'i gzhogs kha brgyad bsdoms pas bcu drug ,rdo rje nag po'i phreng ba phyi nang gnyis bsdoms pa bcu drug ste khyon sum cu so gnyis kyis spyi bo'i rtsa 'dab sum cu so gnyis mtshon, 'khor los dbu skra mi sgrib pa dang, dbu skras 'khor lo mi sgrib par bsgom dgos
rows.english: Each spoke of the circular headdress, as we spoke of above, has an inner and outer section, totaling then 16 pieces.  In our own system though we have a unique way of arriving at this number 16, by adding together the eight spokes of the wheel and the eight facets of the jewels at the top.  We then add another 16 for the two strings of black diamonds, inside and out, which brings us to a total of 32.  This represents the 32 petals of the chakra at the center tip of the head.  In your meditation don't let the headdress block Her hair, nor Her hair block the headdress.

rows.acip: ,CES GNAS SKABS SU LAS KYI SGRIB PA KUN 'DAG PA DANG, LAM 'DI LA BSAM GTAN BYAS PA TZAM DANG, GLEGS BAM BKLAG PA DANG, KHA TON DU BYAS PA DANG RGYUD KYI GLEGS BAM BRIS PAS KYANG MTHO RIS KYI DPAL SPYI DANG, KHYAD PAR BA 'KHOR LOS SGYUR RGYAL 'THOB PAR 'GYUR BAR GSUNGS LA,
rows.wylie: ces gnas skabs su las kyi sgrib pa kun 'dag pa dang, lam 'di la bsam gtan byas pa tsam dang, glegs bam bklag pa dang, kha ton du byas pa dang rgyud kyi glegs bam bris pas kyang mtho ris kyi dpal spyi dang, khyad par ba 'khor los sgyur rgyal 'thob par 'gyur bar gsungs la
rows.english: These lines describe how, in the short run, all of the obstacles caused by one's past deeds are purified.  And anyone who does no more than practice meditative concentration on this path--or who reads the volumes that explain it, or recites them, or writes out books of the secret teaching--by such activity gains in general a glorious life in one of the higher births.  To be more specific, they win a rebirth as one of the Wheel Empowered Emperors of the World.

rows.acip: DE YANG TSOGS GSOG PAR 'DOD NA YAR NGO DANG, SGRIB PA SBYONG BA 'DOD NA MAR NGO ZHES GANG RUNG GCIG GIS CHOG PA 'DRA ZHIG 'DUG KYANG GNYIS KA MA CHAG PA NI GAL CHE'O,,
rows.wylie: de yang tshogs gsog par 'dod na yar ngo dang, sgrib pa sbyong ba 'dod na mar ngo zhes gang rung gcig gis chog pa 'dra zhig 'dug kyang gnyis ka ma chag pa ni gal che'o
rows.english: Now it has been said, correctly, that if you're looking to collect new good karma you can do so powerfully during the Offering of the Tenth that falls during the waxing of the moon; and that if you hope to remove old bad karma it is well done on the Tenth during the moon's waning.  This would seem to imply that you could observe either one of these two; but in truth you should be aware that it's extremely important never to break your observance of both tenth days. The Yoga of Offering Torma Cakes

rows.acip: YI DVAGS DANG DUD 'GRO LA DBANG PO GNYIS SBYOR GYI BDE BA YOD KYANG LAS KYI SGRIB PA CHE ZHING DBANG PO BRTUL BAS BDE BA LAM DU BYED MI NUS PAS SNGAGS BLA MED KYI GDUL BYA'I GTZO BOR MI RUNG,
rows.wylie: yi dvags dang dud 'gro la dbang po gnyis sbyor gyi bde ba yod kyang las kyi sgrib pa che zhing dbang po brtul bas bde ba lam du byed mi nus pas sngags bla med kyi gdul bya'i gtso bor mi rung
rows.english: Craving spirits and animals can experience the bliss of joining together the two sexual organs, but their great obstacles from past actions and their dull intellects prevent them from being able to use this bliss as a path.  As such, they are unfit to be primary aspirants for the unsurpassed secret teaching.

rows.acip: DE NAS SKU'I GNAS THAMS CAD LAS 'OD ZER SNA TSOGS 'PHROS, RANG GI LUS KYI SGO THAMS CAD NAS ZHUGS SGO GSUM GYI SGRIB PA PHRA BA SBYANGS DBANG BZHI PA THOB, RDO RJE GSUM DBYER MI PHYED PA'I DNGOS GRUB THOB PAR BSAM MO,,
rows.wylie: de nas sku'i gnas thams cad las 'od zer sna tshogs 'phros, rang gi lus kyi sgo thams cad nas zhugs sgo gsum gyi sgrib pa phra ba sbyangs dbang bzhi pa thob, rdo rje gsum dbyer mi phyed pa'i dngos grub thob par bsam mo
rows.english: Light rays of a variety of colors fly out then from each of the places on your Lama's holy body; they sink into each of the gateways of your body and purify you of even the most subtle obstacles of body, speech, and mind--you achieve the fourth empowerment.  Imagine then that you have reached the attainment of three diamonds indivisible, one from the other.
