rows.acip: YI GE GSUM NI RDO RJE GSUM GYI MTSON BYED YIN LA, DE GSUM GYIS SGRIB PA GSUM SBYONG BA BZHIN DU, DBANG GSUM GYIS KYANG SBYONG BA 'DRA BA TZAM DANG, DON GYI DBANG BZHI PA RDO RJE GSUM DBYER MI PHYED PAS PHRA BA'I SGRIB PA SBYONG BA LA BSAMS NAS, SNGAR BSHAD PA'I DBANG BZHI THOB PA'I THA SNYAD BYAS PA TZAM YIN GYI, DES DBANG DNGOS THOB PA MIN NO,,
rows.wylie: yi ge gsum ni rdo rje gsum gyi mtshon byed yin la, de gsum gyis sgrib pa gsum sbyong ba bzhin du, dbang gsum gyis kyang sbyong ba 'dra ba tsam dang, don gyi dbang bzhi pa rdo rje gsum dbyer mi phyed pas phra ba'i sgrib pa sbyong ba la bsams nas, sngar bshad pa'i dbang bzhi thob pa'i tha snyad byas pa tsam yin gyi, des dbang dngos thob pa min no
rows.english: The three syllables symbolize the three diamonds; these three purify you of the three obstacles.  The "three empowerments" here are similar, merely representing the same purification.  The ultimate empowerment, the fourth, is where the three diamonds, inseparable, have cleaned you of even your most subtle obstacles.  This is all that is meant when it is stated above that you "receive the four empowerments"; it's not though that by visualizing it you have actually been granted the empowerments themselves.

rows.acip: DES NA STONG NYID KYI DON GTAN LA 'BABS TSUL KHYAD MED KYANG DE'I DON SGOM PAR BYED PA NA, GA-YAS GA-YON GYI RLUNG DH'U T'IR BTZUD NAS DER THIM PA'I DBANG GIS GTUM MO 'BAR BAS BYANG SEMS BZHUS PA'I BDE BA CHEN POS STONG PA'I DON NGES NAS SGOM PA'I LHAN SKYES KYIS SGRIB PA'I BAG CHAGS SBYONG MYUR BA'I NUS PA 'DRA BA YUL CAN GZHAN GANG LA'ANG MED PAS, NGES PAR BDE BA DE BSKYED DGOS SO,,
rows.wylie: des na stong nyid kyi don gtan la 'babs tshul khyad med kyang de'i don sgom par byed pa na, ga-yas ga-yon gyi rlung dhU tIr btsud nas der thim pa'i dbang gis gtum mo 'bar bas byang sems bzhus pa'i bde ba chen pos stong pa'i don nges nas sgom pa'i lhan skyes kyis sgrib pa'i bag chags sbyong myur ba'i nus pa 'dra ba yul can gzhan gang la'ang med pas, nges par bde ba de bskyed dgos so
rows.english: We can say thus that there is no difference between the open and secret teachings on the question of how we establish the fact that everything is empty.  When in the secret teachings we perform a meditation upon this fact, we utilize a feeling of great bliss--bliss which arises when we are able to get the right and left winds into the channel of dance, and dissolve there.  This brings the inner fire to blaze, which melts down the element of enlightenment, bringing on then the great bliss. We use this bliss to perceive the fact that things are empty of themselves.  This simultaneous bliss and voidness, as we meditate with it, has the capacity to rid us quickly of all the propensities we have within us for spiritual obstacles.  There is no other subject state of mind which can compare with this one--combined bliss and emptiness--and so the case is that we absolutely must reach this state of bliss.

rows.acip: DE LTAR SDIG PA THAMS CAD LAS RNAM PAR GROL BAR BYED CING, LUS TE RGYUD DAG PA LAS SKYON MED PA'I MI'I MCHOG KUN NAS GTZANG SBRA'I SPYOD PA BYED PA DE, SDIG PA STE SGRIB PA THAMS CAD RNAM PAR DAG PA'I DE BZHIN GSHEGS PA RDO RJE 'CHANG GI SA 'THOB PAR 'GYUR RO,,
rows.wylie: de ltar sdig pa thams cad las rnam par grol bar byed cing, lus te rgyud dag pa las skyon med pa'i mi'i mchog kun nas gtsang sbra'i spyod pa byed pa de, sdig pa ste sgrib pa thams cad rnam par dag pa'i de bzhin gshegs pa rdo rje 'chang gi sa 'thob par 'gyur ro
rows.english: They too are, in the same way, liberated from all their own bad deeds; their body--which is to say, their mindstream--becomes completely pure.  They then become the immaculate Lord of All Beings, engaging in His own form of purity.  That is, they achieve the state of the One Gone Thus, the Keeper of the Diamond, free of every "bad deed," here meaning "obstacle." * * * On the need for an actual, physical partner, Choney Lama (writing in the 17th century) mentions a disagreement on the matter and expresses his own opinion in the Lamp that Illuminates the Essence: An Explanation of Critical Points in the "Harvest of Attainments" [of Je Tsongkapa], itself a Treatise on the Great, Deep Practice of the Stage of Completion, according to the System of that Great and Accomplished Saint, Luhipa (ACIP digital text S00299, ff. 35b-36a):

rows.acip: GAL TE DE NYON MONGS YIN NA, SGRIB PA YIN DGOS PAS, DE YIN NA RANG GI NGO BO'I SGO NAS BYANG CHUB SGRUB PA LA BAR DU GCOD BYED YIN PA'I PHYIR DE'I RGYUR 'GYUR BA 'GAL LO ZHE NA,
rows.wylie: gal te de nyon mongs yin na, sgrib pa yin dgos pas, de yin na rang gi ngo bo'i sgo nas byang chub sgrub pa la bar du gcod byed yin pa'i phyir de'i rgyur 'gyur ba 'gal lo zhe na
rows.english: One may continue with the following objection: "If something is a mental affliction, then it's necessarily an obstacle to spiritual progress.  And if it's an obstacle like this, then it must be something that, by its very nature, hinders our quest for enlightenment.  And in this case it would be a contradiction to say it were a cause for this enlightenment."

rows.acip: SUM CU RTZA GSUM DANG RGYAL CHEN RIGS BZHI'I LHA RNAMS LA DBANG PO GNYIS SBYOR GYI BDE BA YOD KYANG RLUNG 'DU 'PHROD KYI BDE BA TZAM LAS RTZA DANG KHAMS DKAR DMAR MED PAS DE'I BDE BA MED, YI DVAGS DANG DUD 'GRO LA DBANG PO GNYIS SBYOR GYI BDE BA YOD KYKANG LAS KYI SGRIB PA CHE ZHING DBANG PO RTUL BAS BDE BA LAM DU BYED MI NUS LA,
rows.wylie: sum cu rtsa gsum dang rgyal chen rigs bzhi'i lha rnams la dbang po gnyis sbyor gyi bde ba yod kyang rlung 'du 'phrod kyi bde ba tsam las rtsa dang khams dkar dmar med pas de'i bde ba med, yi dvags dang dud 'gro la dbang po gnyis sbyor gyi bde ba yod kykang las kyi sgrib pa che zhing dbang po rtul bas bde ba lam du byed mi nus la
rows.english: The gods of the Thirty-Three, and the Four Great Kings, do experience the bliss of joining the two organs, but as nothing more than the pleasure of the joining and mixing of the winds.  They do not get the experience of bliss that comes from channels, and the red and white elements, because they do not possess any of these inner parts.  Craving spirits and animals do possess the pleasure of union of the organs, but they have very bad obstacles caused by their past karma and are spiritually very stupid, and thus they are incapable of making this bliss a path.

rows.english: And then we will not come to be infected by these negativities--mental afflictions such as desire and the rest--(which will lead us to the realms of misery, and obstruct our path).

rows.acip: GNYIS PA YAN LAG BDUN PO DE BSAGS SBYANG SPEL GSUM DU 'DU BAR BSTAN PA NI, PHYAG DANG MCHOD PA YI RANG DANG BSKUL BA DANG GSOL 'DEBS LNGA NI, TSOGS GSOGS PA'I YAN LAG ,BSHAGS PA NI SGRIB PA SBYONG BA'I YAN LAG, BSNGO BA NI DGE BA MI ZAD CING GONG 'PHEL DU BYED PA'I YAN LAG GO , (,ZHES YAN LAG BDUN PA 'BUL ZHING, LONG BYUNG TSE, BSHAGS PA'I MTSAMS SU SDOM PA GSUM SO SO'I BSHAGS PA DANG, BLA MA RDOR 'DZIN MA DANG, BYANG CHUB LTUNG BSHAGS SOGS BYA'O,,)
rows.wylie: gnyis pa yan lag bdun po de bsags sbyang spel gsum du 'du bar bstan pa ni, phyag dang mchod pa yi rang dang bskul ba dang gsol 'debs lnga ni, tshogs gsogs pa'i yan lag ,bshags pa ni sgrib pa sbyong ba'i yan lag, bsngo ba ni dge ba mi zad cing gong 'phel du byed pa'i yan lag go , (,zhes yan lag bdun pa 'bul zhing, long byung tshe, bshags pa'i mtshams su sdom pa gsum so so'i bshags pa dang, bla ma rdor 'dzin ma dang, byang chub ltung bshags sogs bya'o,,)
rows.english: This brings us back to our original second point, which is the presentation of a summary of everything into the three points of collecting good deeds; clearing ourselves of obstacles; and increasing the power.  Now the five steps of bowing down to our Lama, making Them offerings, rejoicing in the goodness of all, entreating our Lama to teach, and supplicating Them to stay can all be considered steps where we are collecting good deeds--good karma.  The step of confession is one where we clear ourselves of obstacles.  And then the step of dedication is one where we assure that our good deeds will never wear out, but rather grow ever higher.  Practice thus the Seven Steps.  At the point where you offer your confession, you can--if time permits--confess transgressions of any of the individual vows found in the three sets of commitments; recite the Prayer of the Lama, the Keeper of the Diamond; and go through the Confession of the Downfalls of a Bodhisattva, or other similar practices.

rows.wylie: de nyid ngo bo ji lta bu zhe na, (sgrib med) ste sgrib pa dang bral ba'i (lhan skyes) kyi (dga' ba'i) ngo bor gyur pa'i ye shes kyi rnam par (rol ba dang) ngo bo (dbyer med) pa'i chos kyi dbyings stong pa nyid de
rows.english: "And just what is Their essence?" you may ask.  They are emptiness itself, the Realm of Is, indivisible in Their essence from the divine play of the wisdom whose own essence is that bliss which is simultaneous, free of every obstruction--released from every obstruction there is.

rows.acip: YAN LAG RNAMS LAS RDZAS THA DAD PA'I YAN LAG CAN CHA MED KYIS NYER LEN BYED NA, GDONG GOS KYIS BSGRIBS NA, YAN LAG GZHAN RNAMS KYANG GOS KYIS BSGRIBS PA DANG , GZHAN MA BSGRIBS NA BSGRIBS MA BSGRIBS CHA GNYIS SU YOD PAR 'GYUR BA DANG , BSGRIBS MA BSGRIBS CHA GNYIS YAN LAG RNAMS LA YOD KYI YAN LAG CAN LA MED NA, GDONG GOS KYIS BSGRIBS PA'I TSE YAN LAG CAN GYI GDONG GSAL BAR MTHONG BAR THAL LA,
rows.wylie: yan lag rnams las rdzas tha dad pa'i yan lag can cha med kyis nyer len byed na, gdong gos kyis bsgribs na, yan lag gzhan rnams kyang gos kyis bsgribs pa dang , gzhan ma bsgribs na bsgribs ma bsgribs cha gnyis su yod par 'gyur ba dang , bsgribs ma bsgribs cha gnyis yan lag rnams la yod kyi yan lag can la med na, gdong gos kyis bsgribs pa'i tshe yan lag can gyi gdong gsal bar mthong bar thal la
rows.english: Suppose you say that it's a substance which is a whole, and which has no parts, and which exists distinct from its details, which provides the material cause for the mind. Then when you covered your face with a piece of cloth all the other details of your body would have to be covered as well. If the other details didn't get covered then there would come to be two parts: one that was covered and one that wasn't. These two parts, the covered one and the uncovered one, would be something that applied to the details but not to the whole that had the details. This being the case, you would have to be able to see clearly the face of the whole even when the face as a detail was covered with the cloth.

rows.english: This is a fact, for the actual meaning of Master Dharmakirti's statement is as follows. The Numerist School is describing a situation where you are looking at a physical form either from far away, or from up close. They say that, depending on the distance between you and the object, another physical form which is the result of karma, and which stands between your visual consciousness and the original form, is either clear or not. This then determines whether the original form appears to you distinctly or not. It is not the case though, they say, that what determines whether the original form appears clearly or not is whether or not you have a clear impression of this form. In reply then Master Dharmakirti is asking the Numerists: Let's consider these two cases of some intermediate physical form that comes from karma. Do they, or do they not, function to obscure the two original forms, the one at a distance, and the other close by? If they were to obscure them, then your visual consciousness could never see the two original forms, since they would have been obscured by the others.

rows.english: Suppose your eyes are blocked by some obstruction in them--by particles of dust or something of the like. rows.english: Suppose you let this kind of attitude go on, suppose you fail to apply the spiritual antidotes that would stop these sorts of thoughts. The thoughts then create a kind of spiritual blindness: you begin to get the idea that you are going to be able to stay here in this life, and then you start to obsess on this life. rows.acip: DPE MA GRUB STE MAR ME RANG GIS RANG GSAL BAR BYED PA MA YIN TE MAR ME RANG GIS GSAL BAR BYA BA MIN PA'I PHYIR TE RANG GIS RANG GSAL MI DGOS SHING MI NUS PA'I PHYIR RO, ,DE LTA NA MUN PAS KYANG RANG GZHAN GNYIS KA SGRIB PAR BYED PAR 'GYUR NA DE MI RIGS TE GANG GI PHYIR NA MUN PA LA MUN PAS BSGRIBS PA MED PA'I PHYIR RO, , BSGRIBS NA BUM PA GOS KYIS BSGRIBS PA BZHIN DU MUN PA'ANG MI MTHONG BAR 'GYUR RO, , 'DI DAG NI RTZA SHE LAS GSUNGS PA LTAR RGYAS PAR SHES PAR BYA'O,
rows.wylie: dpe ma grub ste mar me rang gis rang gsal bar byed pa ma yin te mar me rang gis gsal bar bya ba min pa'i phyir te rang gis rang gsal mi dgos shing mi nus pa'i phyir ro, ,de lta na mun pas kyang rang gzhan gnyis ka sgrib par byed par 'gyur na de mi rigs te gang gi phyir na mun pa la mun pas bsgribs pa med pa'i phyir ro, , bsgribs na bum pa gos kyis bsgribs pa bzhin du mun pa'ang mi mthong bar 'gyur ro, , 'di dag ni rtsa she las gsungs pa ltar rgyas par shes par bya'o
rows.english: But your example does not hold true. A lamp is not something which illuminates itself, because it is not something which is the object illuminated by it. There is no need for it to illuminate itself, and it could never do so anyway. If it could, then darkness too shroud both itself and other objects. This though could never be, for the reason that there is no such thing as darkness shrouding darkness. If it did shroud darkness, then it would be like shrouding a vase with a piece of cloth, and we would be unable to see the darkness itself. For these points I am enlarging upon statements found in the Root Text on Wisdom [by the realized being Nagarjuna].

rows.acip: DER THAL, CHOS KYI GRAGS PA'I LUNG DON NI, GRANGS CAN GYIS RGYANG RING THUNG GI GZUGS LA BLTAS PA DE'I TSE NA, RGYANG RING THUNG GI GZUGS DANG , MIG SHES GNYIS KYI BAR DU, LAS GZUGS GSAL MI GSAL SKYE BA'I DBANG GIS, GZUGS GSAL BAR SNANG MI SNANG 'JOG PA YIN GYI, GZUGS KYI RNAM PA SHAR BA'I SGO NAS GZUGS GSAL BAR SNANG MI SNANG 'JOG PA MA YIN ZHES KHAS BLANGS PA LA, DE LTA BU'I LAS GZUGS GNYIS PO DES RGYANG RING THUNG GI GZUGS GNYIS PO DE BSGRIBS SAM MA BSGRIBS, BSGRIBS NA MIG SHES KYIS GZUGS GNYIS PO DE MA MTHONG BAR THAL, DES DE SGRIB PA'I PHYIR,
rows.wylie: der thal, chos kyi grags pa'i lung don ni, grangs can gyis rgyang ring thung gi gzugs la bltas pa de'i tshe na, rgyang ring thung gi gzugs dang , mig shes gnyis kyi bar du, las gzugs gsal mi gsal skye ba'i dbang gis, gzugs gsal bar snang mi snang 'jog pa yin gyi, gzugs kyi rnam pa shar ba'i sgo nas gzugs gsal bar snang mi snang 'jog pa ma yin zhes khas blangs pa la, de lta bu'i las gzugs gnyis po des rgyang ring thung gi gzugs gnyis po de bsgribs sam ma bsgribs, bsgribs na mig shes kyis gzugs gnyis po de ma mthong bar thal, des de sgrib pa'i phyir
rows.english: This is a fact, for the actual meaning of Master Dharmakirti's statement is as follows. The Numerist School is describing a situation where you are looking at a physical form either from far away, or from up close. They say that, depending on the distance between you and the object, another physical form which is the result of karma, and which stands between your visual consciousness and the original form, is either clear or not. This then determines whether the original form appears to you distinctly or not. It is not the case though, they say, that what determines whether the original form appears clearly or not is whether or not you have a clear impression of this form. In reply then Master Dharmakirti is asking the Numerists: Let's consider these two cases of some intermediate physical form that comes from karma. Do they, or do they not, function to obscure the two original forms, the one at a distance, and the other close by? If they were to obscure them, then your visual consciousness could never see the two original forms, since they would have been obscured by the others.

rows.acip: YAN LAG RNAMS LAS RDZAS THA DAD PA'I YAN LAG CAN CHA MED KYIS NYER LEN BYED NA, GDONG GOS KYIS BSGRIBS NA, YAN LAG GZHAN RNAMS KYANG GOS KYIS BSGRIBS PA DANG , GZHAN MA BSGRIBS NA BSGRIBS MA BSGRIBS CHA GNYIS SU YOD PAR 'GYUR BA DANG , BSGRIBS MA BSGRIBS CHA GNYIS YAN LAG RNAMS LA YOD KYI YAN LAG CAN LA MED NA, GDONG GOS KYIS BSGRIBS PA'I TSE YAN LAG CAN GYI GDONG GSAL BAR MTHONG BAR THAL LA,
rows.wylie: yan lag rnams las rdzas tha dad pa'i yan lag can cha med kyis nyer len byed na, gdong gos kyis bsgribs na, yan lag gzhan rnams kyang gos kyis bsgribs pa dang , gzhan ma bsgribs na bsgribs ma bsgribs cha gnyis su yod par 'gyur ba dang , bsgribs ma bsgribs cha gnyis yan lag rnams la yod kyi yan lag can la med na, gdong gos kyis bsgribs pa'i tshe yan lag can gyi gdong gsal bar mthong bar thal la
rows.english: Suppose you say that it's a substance which is a whole, and which has no parts, and which exists distinct from its details, which provides the material cause for the mind. Then when you covered your face with a piece of cloth all the other details of your body would have to be covered as well. If the other details didn't get covered then there would come to be two parts: one that was covered and one that wasn't. These two parts, the covered one and the uncovered one, would be something that applied to the details but not to the whole that had the details. This being the case, you would have to be able to see clearly the face of the whole even when the face as a detail was covered with the cloth.

rows.acip: ,SEMS CAN RNAMS KYI GNAS LUGS NI, ,SEMS DANG DUS MNYAM GNAS DUS NAS, ,YE SANGS RGYAS CIG YIN PA LA, ,'ON KYANG GLO BUR DRI MAS BSGRIBS,
rows.wylie: sems can rnams kyi gnas lugs ni, ,sems dang dus mnyam gnas dus nas, ,ye sangs rgyas cig yin pa la, ,'on kyang glo bur dri mas bsgribs
rows.english: The way of all things Lies here within people; It has lived there part & parcel With their minds since minds began— This is the one primordial Buddha That each of them already is; It's just that this Buddha is veiled By impurities that are not at all Innate parts of the mind. There's some talk going around about how we are already a Buddha inside of us, so we should just relax and let our natural Buddha out.  This is a gross and, eventually, very harmful misunderstanding of the idea of “Buddha nature.” That is, all things possess their inherent emptiness, or the lack of being anything except the end product of our mental seeds, planted by how we treat other people.  This emptiness—in the case of each individual one of us—will remain with us even after we turn into a being who can see everything that is, was, and ever will be in the whole universe. Only in this sense, there is within each of us what will inevitably—in time—become a fully enlightened being.  But we still need to work hard to become the entire package! The final comment here about impurities not being an inherent part of our mind is important.  The best part of the Buddha that we will become is, as we have just shown, an inherent part of our being; but the negative parts of our being are perfectly impermanent and will inevitably be cleaned out.

rows.wylie: [e15] de dag la khyab pa yod de, lus len pa'i rnam shes ni skye ba snga ma'i las kyi mthus tshe ji srid kyi bar du rgyun ma chad par 'jug pa'i rnam smin yin pa dang, rtag tu ma bsgribs lung ma bstan gyi ngo bor gnas pa dang, tshe ji srid kyi bar du lus thams cad la khyab nas 'dzin pa zhig dgos pa'i phyir ro
rows.english: There is a logical necessity within these arguments because, first of all, the consciousness that takes on the body should be one that represents a ripening of karma which occurs through the power of karma committed in a previous lifetime, and should continue on in an unbroken stream for the duration of our life.  Moreover, its fundamental nature should be karmically neutral, of the type which does not cause any spiritual obstacle.  And lastly it should hold its objects even as it extends over the entire body—again for the entire length of our life. Second argument: How could one arise first?

rows.english: Suppose you let this kind of attitude go on, suppose you fail to apply the spiritual antidotes that would stop these sorts of thoughts. The thoughts then create a kind of spiritual blindness: you begin to get the idea that you are going to be able to stay here in this life, and then you start to obsess on this life. All you can concentrate on then is how to get what you want, and how to escape what you don't want, in this life. Your life becomes, “Today I need this, and this, and next this.”

rows.english: This is a fact, for the actual meaning of Master Dharmakirti's statement is as follows. The Numerist School is describing a situation where you are looking at a physical form either from far away, or from up close. They say that, depending on the distance between you and the object, another physical form which is the result of karma, and which stands between your visual consciousness and the original form, is either clear or not. This then determines whether the original form appears to you distinctly or not. It is not the case though, they say, that what determines whether the original form appears clearly or not is whether or not you have a clear impression of this In reply then Master Dharmakirti is asking the Numerists: Let's consider these two cases of some intermediate physical form that comes from karma. Do they, or do they not, function to obscure the two original forms, the one at a distance, and the other close by? If they were to obscure them, then your visual consciousness could never see the two original forms, since they would have been obscured by the others.
